title: Replay engine & scrubbing
body:
## Context
Bybit publishes no historical L2 depth, no historical liquidation feed and only a ~1000-row recent-trade window. Every order-flow claim CandleViewer makes can therefore only be re-examined against **data the product recorded itself** (E16 recorder). E26 turns that recording into a deterministic, seekable time machine, and it is the third R2 goal in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §6.1: "ship deterministic replay so any order-flow claim can be re-examined tick-by-tick, and so R3's trading logic can be tested against reproducible market conditions".

The architectural principle is non-negotiable (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` principle **P2**, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` principle **G6**): **replay is not a parallel implementation**. The replay engine — backend module **M12**, architecture component **C13** — re-emits recorded events onto the *same* bus, through the *same* normalizer -> book engine -> bar builders -> order-flow engines -> WS gateway -> chart pipeline that live traffic uses. The only difference is the clock. That is why replay fidelity is structural rather than aspirational, and why `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.3 exit criterion #1 is verified by a test that replays a recorded day and asserts derived state equals the state captured live.

R3 depends on this epic as a test harness: `30-release-roadmap.md` §12 records "E26 replay … prerequisite for deterministic testing of R3 trading logic … started S11, one train early relative to its consumer". Descoping E26 does not merely lose a feature, it raises QA cost across the whole trading train.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **User stories (all of domain RPL):** US-RPL-001 bar-by-bar replay (Must), US-RPL-002 tick-by-tick replay (Should), US-RPL-003 order-book replay (Should), US-RPL-004 playback controls (Must), US-RPL-005 multi-pane synchronised replay (Should), US-RPL-006 simulated trading during replay (Must), US-RPL-007 replay navigation aids (Should), US-RPL-008 bookmarks and loops (Could), US-RPL-009 replay session state restore (Should).
- **Backend M12** (`apps/api/.../replay/`: `planner`, `source`, `clock`, `injector` per `20-architecture.md` §repo layout): `ReplayPlanner` (window validation against coverage and gaps, tier selection), `ReplaySource` (QuestDB hot reader + Parquet/DuckDB cold reader, k-way merge in `(ts_event, seq)` order), `ReplayClock` (monotonic scheduler, speed 0.1-100x, step modes, backpressure-slows-clock), `Injector` (publishes on `replay.{session_id}.*` through the live chain, env-scoped namespace), `SeekEngine` (snapshot anchor -> delta re-apply -> `BuilderState` checkpoint restore -> metric warm-up), `PaperBridge`.
- **Persistence:** Alembic migration creating `replay_sessions` exactly as specified in `21-database-schema.md` §3.6.4 (including `bookmarks jsonb`, `loop_enabled`, `source_tier`, `cursor_ts`, `gap_warnings`, `events_emitted`, constraints `rps_range`/`rps_speed`/`rps_tier`/`rps_cursor`/`rps_paper`).
- **REST:** `GET /api/v1/replay/sessions`, `POST /api/v1/replay/sessions`, `GET /api/v1/replay/sessions/{replayId}`, `DELETE /api/v1/replay/sessions/{replayId}`, `POST /api/v1/replay/sessions/{replayId}/control`; consumption of `GET /api/v1/market/data-coverage` (owned by E16).
- **WS:** `replay_session_id` on `sub` (`23-ws-protocol.md` §11), `source: "replay"` in `snap` metadata plus binary header flag bit2, `rs` in the envelope, `wt` wall-clock field on replay frames, `snap` with `reason: "replay_seek"`, `revoked` with `reason: "replay_session_ended"`, rejection of private topics with `invalid_options`, error codes `replay_session_not_found` and `replay_session_ended`.
- **Screens:** SCR-097 Replay page, SCR-098 Replay session setup modal, SCR-099 Replay paper-trading results; SCR-044 "Go to date" dialog reused for jump-to-timestamp.
- **Components:** CMP-170 ReplayScrubber, CMP-171 ReplaySpeedPicker, CMP-172 ReplayRangePicker (new design-system entries), plus reuse of CMP-180, CMP-196, CMP-028, CMP-035, CMP-043, CMP-047, CMP-219, CMP-026, CMP-027.
- **ADR-0018** Replay determinism, seek strategy and resource governance.
- Design track E26-D01..D08, QA track E26-Q01..Q06, security track E26-X01..X03.

## Out of scope
- The recorder, retention policies, snapshot cadence and the `GET /market/data-coverage` implementation — owned by **E16**.
- Bar builders, footprint, profiles, DOM ladder/heatmap, CVD and detectors — they are *consumed unmodified*. If a downstream engine turns out not to be replay-safe, that is a Bug on the owning epic (E12/E18/E19/E21/E23/E25), not scope here.
- The paper matcher fill model, queue-position modelling and demo/live parity — **E38**. E26 ships only the replay-side bridge plus the isolation invariant.
- Rule-engine simulation/backtesting over replay — **E35**.
- Backtesting over synthetic or generated (non-recorded) data.
- Android / mobile clients (out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14); no separate admin app.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One code path proven, not asserted
  Given a recorded symbol-day whose live-derived bars, footprint cells, profile levels and deterministic metrics were captured at record time
  When that day is replayed end to end through the replay engine
  Then every derived value equals the live-captured value (tolerance 0 for exact metrics, 1e-9 for floats)
  And any difference fails CI

Scenario: Determinism across runs and machines
  Given the same recorded window is replayed twice, once on a developer machine and once on CI
  Then the emitted event stream and every derived series are byte-identical
  And the detector event stream is identical (roadmap exit criterion #7)

Scenario: Seek within budget
  Given a 200-depth recorded symbol-day
  When the user scrubs to an arbitrary timestamp inside the loaded window
  Then book, footprint and CVD state are reconstructed correctly and rendered within 1 s at p95, with a 2 s hard ceiling

Scenario: Replay can never be mistaken for live, and can never reach the exchange
  Given a replay session is playing with paper fills enabled
  Then every replaying pane shows the REPLAY chrome, clock and badge
  And every simulated fill is tagged simulated=true and recorded in the replay journal only
  And no replay-sourced event can be routed to a live or demo exchange account

Scenario: Missing coverage is stated, never silently skipped
  Given the requested window intersects a recording_gaps row
  When the session is created
  Then the gap is reported up front and again when playback reaches it, with Skip gap and Stop here options
```

## Technical notes / design
`24-internal-schemas.md` §13.7 is the authoritative specification. Seek algorithm: (1) find the latest `orderbook_snapshot` at or before the target (written every `snapshot_interval_s`, default 300 s, plus on every subscribe/resync); (2) rebuild the book from it; (3) re-apply book deltas up to the target; (4) restore bar/footprint/profile state from a persisted `BuilderState` checkpoint (written every 60 s per `(symbol, spec_hash)`) or replay trades from the enclosing session anchor; (5) prime metric warm-up by replaying `max(warmup_bars)` bars before the target so indicators are valid at t=0 rather than `None`.

Playback: a monotonic scheduler emits events preserving inter-event deltas scaled by `speed`. `speed=0` is step mode (`step_event`, `step_ms(n)`, `step_bar`); `speed=-1` emits as fast as consumers accept (used by rule backtests). **Backpressure slows the clock rather than dropping events — replay must never lose data**; the achieved rate is reported to the client instead (US-RPL-002 NFR).

`ExecutionMode` is `"replay"` internally and never crosses the wire as an `Environment` (`24-internal-schemas.md` §2); replay is distinguished on the wire only by the frame's `source: "replay"` marker.

## Test plan
Golden-file determinism suite over a version-controlled recorded fixture; double-run equality; seek-correctness property tests; OpenAPI + WS §11 contract tests; Playwright E2E on SCR-097/098/099 (web and Electron); replay-soak at 100x over a recorded 24 h fixture (budget #15); chaos over gaps, pruned data, slow consumers, session expiry and server restart; axe-core CI plus a manual screen-reader pass. Coverage >=85% on the backend replay package, >=80% on the web replay feature.

## Security notes
STRIDE per `04-security-program.md`. Threat **S3** (replay/export endpoint used to read arbitrary filesystem paths) is rated High: mitigated by **SR-097** — no user-supplied filesystem paths anywhere in the replay API, datasets addressed only by registry ids, with mandatory path-traversal and symlink-escape tests. **Resource exhaustion**: an unbounded window at 100x is a denial of service against the trading host — per-user concurrent-session quota, window-size cap, per-session memory ceiling and 2 h idle reclaim. RBAC `replay:read` / `replay:write`, scope `self`. Private topics (`orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet`) are never replayable. Paper fills inside replay are tagged `simulated=true` and never enter the trading audit stream. Data classification A-10 (recorded market data), integrity objective O8.

## Accessibility notes
The replay clock is a labelled live region updated at most 1 Hz; the scrubber is `role="slider"` with `aria-valuetext` in absolute human-readable time; transport controls are standard labelled buttons carrying shortcut hints; REPLAY state is conveyed by text and iconography, never by colour alone; the full hotkey table of SCR-097 is keyboard-reachable and documented in Storybook.

## Performance notes
Budget #2 (frame time <=16.6 ms p95, never below 30 fps, worst case explicitly includes "replay at 20x") and budget #15 (sustain up to 100x crash-free; visual fidelity may degrade by skip-render but must not desync) from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`. SCR-097 additionally requires 25x on 1-minute data and 4x on raw tick data without dropped frames, and seek <=1 s within the loaded window. SCR-098 requires a 1-day single-symbol session ready in <=10 s with progress shown.

## Observability
Metrics: `replay_sessions_active`, `replay_events_emitted_total`, `replay_clock_lag_ms`, `replay_seek_duration_ms`, `replay_source_tier`, `replay_gap_warnings_total`, `replay_backpressure_seconds_total`, `replay_session_memory_bytes`. Trace: OpenTelemetry span for replay session start (one of the two traced paths in `20-architecture.md` §observability). Analytics/audit: `replay.session_created`, `replay.started`, `replay.seek`, `replay.session_deleted`, `replay.paper_fill`, `replay.results_viewed`, `replay.results_promoted_to_journal`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child Story/Task/Spike/Design/QA/Security ticket is Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded Won't/Later disposition.
- [ ] Roadmap §6.3 exit criteria #1 (single shared pipeline), #7 (detector reproducibility) and #8 (determinism + 1 s scrub) demonstrated by CI checks, not by claim.
- [ ] Coverage floors held (>=85% backend/engine, >=80% frontend); zero open P0/P1 bugs in E26 scope.
- [ ] ADR-0018 merged; `20-architecture.md`, `24-internal-schemas.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md`, `14-screens-catalogue.md` reconciled with shipped behaviour.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core green on SCR-097/098/099 plus a manual screen-reader pass recorded.
- [ ] perf: budgets #2 and #15 recorded; seek p95 <1 s recorded in the benchmark report.
- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, findings triaged (fixed or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off), Security engineer sign-off comment present.
- [ ] Epic-level QA regression and exploratory pass executed and recorded; design QA sign-off from the CDO track; demoed to Owner at Sprint Review against staging (demo).

## Dependencies
- **E16** recorder, retention and `GET /market/data-coverage` — supplies the recorded streams, the periodic `orderbook_snapshot` seek anchors and the gap records. Without it there is nothing to replay.
- **E17** WS protocol and binary framing — supplies the `replay_session_id` routing hook, the `source`/`rs`/`wt` envelope fields and header flag bit2.
- **E12** bar builders — the `BarBuilder.snapshot()`/`restore()` contract and `spec_hash` determinism property (invariant BI-4) underpin seek.
- **E18**, **E21** — the order-flow surfaces replay must reproduce identically; the determinism harness diffs against their live-captured output.
- **E38** paper trading — supplies the `PaperMatcher` consumed by E26-S07; the replay-side bridge ships flagged off until E38 lands.

## Branch
`feat/replay-engine-<short>` per child ticket (e.g. `feat/replay-engine-clock`). PRs <=400 LOC diff preferred; the engine tasks split along planner/source/clock/seek boundaries to hold that.

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: UX research: how traders study a recorded session and what replay must not hide
body:
## Context
Replay is a *study* tool, not a playback toy: the trader is trying to answer "why did this move happen and would I have seen it live?". Getting the interaction wrong in either direction is expensive — too little control and the tool is useless for post-mortems (US-RPL-007 navigation aids exist precisely because scrubbing blindly through a day finds nothing), too much chrome and the study surface competes with the chart it exists to explain.

Two risks make research mandatory before pixels. First, **replay-vs-live confusion**: SCR-097's sign-off explicitly requires "REPLAY chrome cannot be confused with live", and a trader who mistakes replay for live can act on stale prices. Second, **recorder-dependent emptiness** (`14-screens-catalogue.md` §global conventions rule 3): replay depth equals recorder depth, so the honest empty/partial states are the normal case in the first weeks, not an edge case.

This ticket produces the evidence that D02-D05 design against. It is scheduled in Sprint 07 so that the hi-fi work lands in the D-S08 design sprint (`30-release-roadmap.md` §1.2, "Replay UI, alerts UI"), two sprints ahead of the E26 frontend stories in Sprint 11+.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Structured sessions with the Owner and the two account managers (the entire real user population) covering: how they currently post-mortem a trade; what they would step through tick-by-tick versus scan at speed; what "notable moment" means to them (feeding US-RPL-007's event-jump list).
- Competitive teardown of replay UX in TradingView Bar Replay, ATAS and Sierra Chart: transport layout, speed affordances, how each signals replay mode, how each handles missing data.
- A findings memo committed at `docs/research/ux/replay-study-sessions.md` with: the ranked task list, the moment-finding vocabulary, and a recommendation on default speed presets measured against the catalogue set (0.5x/1x/2x/4x/10x/25x/100x on SCR-097 vs CMP-171's 0.5x/1x/2x/5x/10x/25x/50x/100x — the discrepancy must be resolved here and the winner written back into `15-component-catalogue.md`).
- A decision on the replay-mode signalling pattern (chrome border + clock + badge) to be validated in D06's a11y review, including a colour-blind-safe and a reduced-chrome variant.
- Concrete answers, recorded as design constraints for D02: does the trader want live panes beside replaying panes (US-RPL-005 opt-out), and is paper trading in replay (US-RPL-006) expected to feel like the real ticket or a deliberately distinct surface?

## Out of scope
- Any hi-fi or wireframe artefact (D02-D05).
- Recorder configuration UX — E16-D01 covered that; this ticket reuses its findings on recorder mental models rather than re-running them.
- Journal/analytics study flows (E41).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Findings are evidence, not opinion
  Given the research sessions are complete
  When the memo is reviewed by the CDO and the E26 tech lead
  Then every design recommendation in it cites at least one observed session moment or a competitor teardown finding
  And open questions are listed explicitly rather than resolved by assumption

Scenario: The speed-preset discrepancy is closed
  Given SCR-097 lists 0.5x/1x/2x/4x/10x/25x/100x and CMP-171 lists 0.5x/1x/2x/5x/10x/25x/50x/100x
  When the memo is signed off
  Then one canonical preset list is chosen with a stated rationale
  And a doc-reconciliation action is filed against E26-T07

Scenario: Replay-mode signalling is validated with users
  Given at least two candidate signalling treatments
  When participants are shown a screenshot for 2 seconds and asked "is this live?"
  Then the chosen treatment is identified correctly by every participant
  And the result is recorded in the memo
```

## Technical notes / design
Constraints to carry into the sessions: replay reuses the terminal's dockable panel set (SCR-097 wireframe), so the transport bar is the only net-new chrome on the study surface; sessions are server-side objects with a 2 h idle reclaim; speeds above 25x disable paper fills (SCR-097 validation rules); the scrubber's track must render recorded / partial / missing coverage from `GET /market/data-coverage`.

## Test plan
N/A for automated tests. Validation method: moderated think-aloud, 5 tasks per participant (start a session over a known window, find the biggest print of the hour, step back through a trade, discover a recorder gap, resume yesterday's session). Success threshold recorded per task.

## Security notes
Research artefacts must not include real API keys, account identifiers or balances; screenshots used in the memo are taken against the demo environment with synthetic accounts. Data classification: none beyond internal.

## Accessibility notes
At least one participant session includes keyboard-only operation of the current chart surface, to inform the transport-control hotkey map before it is drawn. The signalling recommendation must not rely on colour alone (WCAG 2.2 AA, `05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Performance notes
Research must surface the perceived-latency expectation for scrub (users typically expect "instant"); record the tolerance observed so D02 can design the honest seeking state against the 1 s p95 / 2 s ceiling budget rather than pretending seek is free.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Memo merged at `docs/research/ux/replay-study-sessions.md` and linked from this ticket.
- [ ] Canonical speed-preset list decided; doc-reconciliation action filed against E26-T07.
- [ ] Replay-mode signalling recommendation validated and recorded.
- [ ] CDO sign-off comment recorded; findings presented at the design review.
- [ ] Open questions either answered or converted into explicit design assumptions carried on E26-D02.

## Dependencies
`E16-D01` established the recorder mental model and the auto-record surprise findings; this ticket builds on them rather than repeating them.

## Branch
`design/replay-ux-research` (artefacts and memo only; no product code).

title: Wireframe to hi-fi SCR-097 replay page: transport, coverage scrubber, states
body:
## Context
SCR-097 (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §7) is the primary surface of this epic and the one screen where a visual mistake has a trading consequence: its sign-off checklist opens with "REPLAY chrome cannot be confused with live". The page hosts the same dockable panel set as the terminal, fed by the replay clock, plus a transport bar; everything else the trader sees is an existing order-flow panel rendering replay frames through the identical pipeline (`23-ws-protocol.md` G6).

Delivered in design sprint D-S08 ("Replay UI, alerts UI", `30-release-roadmap.md` §1.2) so it is Done at least two sprints before the consuming frontend story E26-S02 in Sprint 11.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Wireframe then hi-fi Figma frames for **SCR-097** at all supported densities and in both themes, matching the catalogue wireframe: header line (`REPLAY  <SYMBOL>  <timestamp to ms>  speed Nx`), the panel region, the transport row (`|<<  <  [PLAY]  >  >>|`), the speed picker, the scrub track with a time axis, and the option row (`[x] paper fills  [ ] keep live panes  bookmarks: #42 #43`).
- The **REPLAY chrome variant**: border treatment, clock typography (monospace, ms precision), badge placement on every replaying pane, and the visual relationship to the demo/live environment badge so the two never read as one thing.
- The **coverage scrubber**: recorded / partial / missing shading on the track, bookmark markers, the playhead, and the drag-seek affordance including the "seeking" state.
- Every state from the catalogue: configuring, buffering, playing, paused, seeking, **gap encountered** ("No data 13:52-13:55 - recorder was offline. [Skip gap] [Stop here]"), end of range, paper-fill mode active, session expired (server reclaims after 2 h idle, with a resume option).
- The **speed-limit honesty state**: when the engine cannot sustain the requested rate it must show the achieved rate rather than silently dropping (US-RPL-002 performance scenario), and speeds above 25x must visibly disable paper fills with the reason.
- The hotkey overlay contribution for the Replay context group in SCR-030 (`Space`, `<-/->`, `Shift+<-/->`, `Ctrl+<-/->`, `R`, `B`, `[`/`]`).
- Redlines: spacing, tokens, type ramp, focus rings, hit targets for the transport buttons and the scrub thumb.

## Out of scope
- SCR-098 (E26-D03) and SCR-099 (E26-D04).
- The CMP-170/171/172 design-system entries themselves (E26-D05) — this ticket specifies usage in context and hands the component contract to D05.
- Motion specification and the a11y design review (E26-D06).
- Order-flow panel design — already owned by E18/E19/E20/E21/E22/E23/E24; replay renders them unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Replay chrome passes the two-second test
  Given the hi-fi frames for playing replay and for the live terminal
  When five reviewers are shown each for two seconds
  Then all five correctly identify which is replay
  And the identification does not depend on colour alone

Scenario: Every catalogue state is drawn
  Given the SCR-097 states list in 14-screens-catalogue.md
  When the frame set is reviewed against it
  Then configuring, buffering, playing, paused, seeking, gap-encountered, end-of-range, paper-fill-active and session-expired each have a frame
  And the gap state shows the exact missing range with Skip gap and Stop here actions

Scenario: The scrubber tells the truth about coverage
  Given a window with a 3-minute recorder gap and a partially covered tail
  When the scrub track is rendered
  Then recorded, partial and missing segments are distinguishable without colour alone
  And the earliest available timestamp is stated in text

Scenario: Seeking is designed as a real cost
  Given the seek budget is 1 s p95 with a 2 s ceiling
  When the seeking state is drawn
  Then it shows determinate or explained progress rather than an unbounded spinner
```

## Technical notes / design
Data bindings to design against: `POST /api/v1/replay/sessions` returns `{ id, state, symbols, from, to, cursor_ts, speed, streams, depth, paper_account_id, progress_pct }`; `state` is the Postgres `replay_state` enum `created|buffering|playing|paused|finished|error` (`21-database-schema.md` §3.6.4), and the frames must map 1:1 to those values plus the client-only `seeking` condition. Playback control is `POST /api/v1/replay/sessions/{replayId}/control` with actions `play|pause|seek|step` (`step` carries exactly one of `step_events` or `step_ms`). Coverage shading comes from `GET /api/v1/market/data-coverage?symbol`.

## Test plan
Design validation only: prototype walkthrough of start -> play -> scrub -> hit gap -> bookmark -> end of range -> resume. Discrepancies against the built screen are caught by E26-D08 design QA and E26-Q05 a11y audit.

## Security notes
The frames must never show a real account identifier or balance. The paper-fill option must be drawn so that "simulated" is structurally unmissable — this is the visual half of the isolation invariant enforced technically in E26-S07 and reviewed in E26-X03.

## Accessibility notes
Specify: the clock as a labelled live region updated at most 1 Hz (not per frame); the scrub track as `role="slider"` with `aria-valuetext` in absolute time; visible focus on every transport control; a text equivalent for coverage shading; contrast >=4.5:1 for the REPLAY chrome text and >=3:1 for its non-text indicator, per `05-accessibility-standard.md`. Formal review is E26-D06.

## Performance notes
Design the transport for a clock that updates at most 1 Hz for assistive tech while the visual readout may update per frame; avoid per-frame layout thrash in the scrub track by specifying a fixed-width monospace timestamp field.

## Observability
Annotate the frames with the analytics events they emit: `replay.started`, `replay.seek`, `replay.paper_fill`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Figma frames published, versioned and linked on this ticket; redlines complete.
- [ ] Every state in the SCR-097 catalogue entry has a frame; the catalogue entry updated if a state was added or renamed during design.
- [ ] The SCR-097 design sign-off acceptance checklist in `14-screens-catalogue.md` is fully satisfied and ticked with evidence.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded; Status Done at least two sprints before E26-S02 starts.

title: Hi-fi SCR-098 replay setup modal with coverage timeline and honest preparation
body:
## Context
SCR-098 is where the recorder-dependency becomes visible to the trader: a replay session can only exist over a window the recorder actually covered. `14-screens-catalogue.md` §global rule 3 requires recorder-dependent emptiness to be a *designed state* naming the first available timestamp, never a blank canvas, and the SCR-098 validation rules require "Nothing is recorded for that window." rather than a generic error. US-RPL-001's third scenario goes further: when the chosen start precedes available data, **the earliest available timestamp is offered instead, with the reason stated** — an offer, not a rejection.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi Figma for **SCR-098** (modal): symbol multiselect (CMP-219 SymbolPicker), date/time range with the coverage timeline (CMP-172 ReplayRangePicker, CMP-047 DateRangePicker), starting speed (CMP-171), panel-inclusion checklist, paper-trading toggle with starting balance and account selection, and the "start from a journal trade / alert / rule firing" shortcuts.
- The **coverage timeline** presentation: recorded, partial and missing windows on one track, with the total recorded depth stated in text ("History starts 2026-09-01 - recording began then").
- States: coverage loading, no coverage (CMP-026 EmptyState with a route to the recorder screen SCR-140 for owners and an explanatory read-only message otherwise), partial coverage warning, validation error (CMP-027).
- **Preparation progress**: a 1-day single-symbol session must be ready in <=10 s with progress shown; larger requests must state the estimated preparation time *before* starting, with a cancel affordance.
- The resume path for US-RPL-009: an existing saved session for this symbol is offered ("Resume 2026-09-10 13:00 at 13:38, speed 4x") alongside "Start fresh", plus the data-changed variant ("the underlying data was pruned since - nearest available start is X").
- The paper-trading copy: "Paper trading only - nothing reaches the exchange."
- Redlines and the full form validation message set.

## Out of scope
- SCR-097 (E26-D02), SCR-099 (E26-D04), the CMP design-system entries (E26-D05).
- The recorder admin screens SCR-140/141/142 (E16).
- Journal/alert/rule entry points' own surfaces — this ticket designs only the inbound shortcut in the modal.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A window with no coverage is refused helpfully
  Given the user picks a range that does not intersect any recorded coverage
  When validation runs
  Then the modal states that nothing is recorded for that window
  And it names the nearest recorded range and offers to use it

Scenario: A start before available history becomes an offer
  Given the chosen start precedes the earliest recorded timestamp
  When the user attempts to continue
  Then the earliest available timestamp is offered as a substitute with the reason stated
  And the user can accept it in one action

Scenario: Preparation cost is stated, not discovered
  Given a request spanning three symbols over a full day
  When the user submits
  Then the estimated preparation time is shown before preparation starts
  And a cancel control is available throughout

Scenario: Resuming a pruned session is explained
  Given a saved replay position whose underlying data has since been pruned
  When the modal opens
  Then it states what changed and offers the nearest available start point
```

## Technical notes / design
Bindings: `GET /api/v1/market/data-coverage?symbol` for the timeline; `POST /api/v1/replay/sessions` with `{ symbols, from, to, speed, streams, depth, paper_account_id, autostart }`; a window lacking coverage is rejected server-side with `no_data_recorded` (422), so the modal must pre-empt that error rather than surface it raw. `speed` is constrained 0.1-100 by `rps_speed`; `range_end > range_start` by `rps_range`; `paper_trading = false OR paper_account_id IS NOT NULL` by `rps_paper` (`21-database-schema.md` §3.6.4) — each constraint needs a human-language message, not a constraint name.

## Test plan
Prototype walkthrough: no coverage, partial coverage, start-before-history, resume-existing, resume-after-prune, paper toggle without an account selected. Verified against the built screen in E26-D08.

## Security notes
The paper-account selector must only list accounts the caller has been granted (`04-security-program.md` RBAC scope `granted_accounts`); the design must not imply the user can replay another user's sessions (`replay:read` is scoped `self`). No filesystem path input appears anywhere in this modal — datasets are addressed by symbol and time range only (SR-097).

## Accessibility notes
A standard labelled form: date-time range, symbol multiselect, speed, paper account. The available-history statement is text adjacent to the range field, not a tooltip. Validation errors name their field and are associated via `aria-describedby`. The coverage timeline needs a text alternative listing recorded ranges. Formal review in E26-D06.

## Performance notes
Coverage data must be fetched once per symbol selection and cached for the modal's lifetime; the design must not imply a fetch per drag frame on the range control.

## Observability
Annotate `replay.session_created {range, symbols, speed}` and `replay.session_deleted`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Figma frames published with redlines; every catalogue state drawn.
- [ ] The SCR-098 design sign-off checklist in `14-screens-catalogue.md` fully satisfied with evidence.
- [ ] All server-side validation failures have a designed human-language message.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded; Done >=2 sprints before E26-S01.

## Dependencies
`E26-D02` fixes the shared visual language (chrome, coverage shading, speed picker) this modal inherits.

## Branch
`design/replay-scr098`.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md#23-rpl--replay` — US-RPL-001 .. US-RPL-009
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` — SCR-097 Replay page, SCR-098 Replay session setup modal, SCR-099 Replay paper-trading results, SCR-044 "Go to date" dialog
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` — CMP-170 ReplayScrubber, CMP-171 ReplaySpeedPicker, CMP-172 ReplayRangePicker, CMP-180 ChartRoot, CMP-196 MultiChartLinker, CMP-028, CMP-035, CMP-043, CMP-047, CMP-219, CMP-026, CMP-027

title: Hi-fi SCR-099 replay paper-trading results with simulated framing throughout
body:
## Context
SCR-099 shows the outcome of rehearsing execution inside replay (US-RPL-006). It is the single highest-risk screen in the epic for **honesty**, because it presents P&L numbers that are entirely modelled. `14-screens-catalogue.md` §SCR-099 requires the simulated framing on every figure, the fill-model assumptions stated explicitly (queue position, latency, slippage model), and the caveat that these results are not a backtest guarantee. Risk R12 (backtest bias) and the product's advice-boundary stance (R9) both land here.

`24-internal-schemas.md` §12 defines the modelled behaviour these assumptions must describe: the L2-aware fill model walks the reconstructed book with a default 80 ms latency penalty, limit orders fill when prints cross the level *and* the estimated queue position is consumed, and a market order can be rejected with `INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY` when the book is exhausted.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi Figma for **SCR-099** (end-of-session drawer): simulated fill list, P&L, R distribution, the equity curve (CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart), the summary stats card (CMP-168 JournalStatsSummaryCard), the P&L badge (CMP-116 PnLBadge), the export bar (CMP-099 PrintExportBar) and the results table (CMP-049 Table).
- The **assumptions block**: latency model and its value, slippage model, queue-position assumption, and the book source (replayed recorded depth at the configured tier), each in plain language with the configured value shown rather than described generically.
- The **simulated framing**: the badge lives in the heading, not only as a chip (catalogue a11y requirement); every figure carries the framing; the "these results are not a backtest guarantee" caveat is non-dismissible.
- The **promote-to-journal** flow: saving writes journal entries flagged `simulated=true`, excluded from live analytics by default, with the confirmation copy making the exclusion explicit.
- The **opt-in comparison** against the same period's real trades, drawn as clearly separated and off by default.
- Empty state (no simulated fills in the session) and error state (results computation failed).

## Out of scope
- The paper matcher's fill model itself (E38) — this ticket only *presents* its assumptions.
- Journal and analytics screens (E41); SCR-099 links into them.
- SCR-097 and SCR-098.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No figure appears without its framing
  Given the results drawer with a positive simulated P&L
  When any numeric figure is reviewed
  Then it is within a region whose heading carries the simulated framing
  And the non-dismissible caveat is present in the drawer

Scenario: Assumptions are concrete
  Given the session ran with the default 80 ms latency penalty and the L2-aware fill model
  When the assumptions block is rendered
  Then the actual configured latency value and model name are shown, not a generic description

Scenario: Promoting to the journal states the consequence
  Given the user chooses to save the session to the journal
  When the confirmation appears
  Then it states that entries are flagged simulated and excluded from live analytics by default

Scenario: Real-trade comparison cannot be mistaken for the simulated result
  Given the opt-in comparison is enabled
  Then simulated and real series are visually and textually separated, and distinguishable without colour alone
```

## Technical notes / design
Results are computed server-side at session end and fetched once; no live subscriptions remain open (catalogue performance note). Charts must each have a table alternative. `is_paper`/`simulated=true` is the persisted marker (`24-internal-schemas.md` §2: `ExecutionMode` is internal, `is_paper` is what is persisted and published), and the environment stays its real value (`demo`, or `live` when replaying live-recorded data) because environment and paper-ness are orthogonal — the design must not collapse them into a single "replay environment" label.

## Test plan
Prototype walkthrough: profitable session, losing session, zero-fill session, rejected-for-liquidity fill present, promote-to-journal, enable comparison. Built-screen verification in E26-D08.

## Security notes
The promote-to-journal action is audited as `journal.simulated_import`; the design must show that it is a recorded action. Simulated results must never be exportable in a form that omits the simulated flag — the export bar's output format is specified to include it.

## Accessibility notes
Results are a table plus a summary description list; every chart has a table alternative; the simulated badge is in the heading so screen-reader users meet it before the numbers. Contrast and focus per `05-accessibility-standard.md`. Formal review in E26-D06.

## Performance notes
Single fetch at session end; the drawer must render within the standard panel-open budget with up to 500 simulated fills, with virtualisation specified beyond that.

## Observability
`replay.results_viewed`, `replay.results_exported`, `replay.results_promoted_to_journal` (writes journal entries flagged `simulated=true`, audited as `journal.simulated_import`).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Figma frames published with redlines; all states drawn.
- [ ] The SCR-099 design sign-off checklist in `14-screens-catalogue.md` fully satisfied with evidence.
- [ ] Assumption copy reviewed and approved by the E38 paper-trading lead for factual accuracy.

title: Design-system entries for CMP-170, CMP-171 and CMP-172 replay components
body:
## Context
The three replay components are new design-system entries, not one-off screen parts: DoR for any Story with UI requires that "component(s) used are in `15-component-catalogue.md`; any new component has a design-system entry, not an ad hoc one-off" (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1). CMP-170 is an organism whose keyboard contract *is* the replay hotkey table, so it must be specified once and reused rather than reimplemented per screen.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CMP-170 ReplayScrubber** (organism, trading/chart-adjacent): all variants from the catalogue Storybook list — Paused, Playing, HighSpeed, WithBookmarks, KeyboardControlDemo — plus the states D02 introduced: Seeking, GapAhead, EndOfRange, SessionExpired. Props contract per the catalogue API sketch: `currentTime`, `range {from,to}`, `speed`, `playing`, `bookmarks?`, `onPlayPause`, `onSpeedChange`, `onScrub(time)`, `onStepBar(dir)`, `onStepTick(dir)`, `onJumpToRealtime`. Specify the coverage-shading extension needed by SCR-097 and write the prop back into the catalogue.
- **CMP-171 ReplaySpeedPicker** (molecule): the canonical preset list decided in E26-D01, the custom-value affordance required by US-RPL-004 ("plus a custom value"), and the disabled-with-reason treatment for speeds above 25x when paper fills are on.
- **CMP-172 ReplayRangePicker** (molecule): Default, PartialAvailability and NoRecordedHistory(EmptyState) variants, with the recorder-availability shading rule ("only recorded ranges are selectable").
- Token usage: `color.action.primary` and `font.mono` for the timestamp/speed readout per the catalogue entries; specify the coverage-state tokens (recorded / partial / missing) as design-system additions rather than local colours.
- Storybook story list and the keyboard table for CMP-170 documenting `Space` play/pause, `<-/->` step bar, `Shift+<-/->` step tick, `Ctrl+<-/->` jump 1 minute, `R` jump to real time, `B` bookmark, `[`/`]` previous/next bookmark.
- Updates to `15-component-catalogue.md` for every contract change made here.

## Out of scope
- Implementation of the components (E26-S02 builds them against this spec).
- Screen composition (D02/D03/D04).
- Motion curves and reduced-motion behaviour (E26-D06).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The scrubber contract covers every consumer
  Given SCR-097 needs coverage shading and SCR-098 needs range selection
  When the CMP-170 and CMP-172 contracts are reviewed
  Then each required capability maps to a named prop or documented variant
  And no screen needs a local fork of the component

Scenario: The hotkey table is single-sourced
  Given the SCR-097 hotkeys in 14-screens-catalogue.md
  When the CMP-170 Storybook keyboard table is reviewed
  Then it matches the screen catalogue exactly
  And any divergence is resolved in the catalogue, not in the component

Scenario: Speed presets are canonical
  Given the decision recorded in E26-D01
  When CMP-171 is specified
  Then its preset list matches the decision and 15-component-catalogue.md is updated to match
```

## Technical notes / design
The scrub thumb must meet the minimum pointer target size and the track must remain operable at the smallest supported density; specify the hit-area expansion rather than relying on the visual track height. `aria-valuetext` shows the human-readable timestamp, not a raw epoch number (catalogue a11y requirement).

## Test plan
Design-system review board sign-off; Storybook story list agreed with the frontend lead so E26-S02 can implement against it. Component unit/visual/axe/keyboard/performance tests are listed in the catalogue entries and are implemented with the components.

## Security notes
N/A — presentational components with no privileged data. They must not embed account identifiers in accessible names.

## Accessibility notes
CMP-170: transport controls are standard labelled buttons; the scrub bar is `role="slider"` with `aria-valuetext`; the full hotkey table is documented. CMP-172: availability shading requires a non-colour carrier and a text summary of available ranges. All three: visible focus, 4.5:1 text contrast, 3:1 non-text contrast.

## Performance notes
Specify that the scrubber's timestamp readout uses a fixed-width monospace field so a per-frame update causes no reflow, and that scrub drag is throttled to one seek request per settle rather than per pointer move.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Figma component specs published; `15-component-catalogue.md` updated for CMP-170/171/172.
- [ ] Storybook story list and keyboard table agreed with the frontend lead.
- [ ] Design-system board sign-off recorded.

title: Motion spec and accessibility design review for the replay transport and chrome
body:
## Context
Replay is the one surface where motion is the content: the playhead moves, the clock ticks, panes animate at up to 100x. Unreviewed, that becomes both an accessibility hazard (vestibular triggers, a live region that fires hundreds of times a second) and a performance hazard (per-frame DOM updates competing with the WebGL frame budget). `05-accessibility-standard.md` mandates WCAG 2.2 AA with reduced-motion respect; `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-097 caps the clock live region at 1 Hz.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Motion spec** for: playhead advance, scrub drag and settle, the seeking state, the play/pause state change, bookmark marker appearance, gap-encountered attention, and the REPLAY chrome entry/exit when a session starts and ends. Durations, easings and the exact `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback for each (which reduce to instant, which reduce to a cross-fade).
- The **speed-dependent motion rule**: above a stated multiplier, decorative motion is suppressed entirely so that frame budget is spent on the chart, not on chrome animation.
- **Accessibility design review** of SCR-097, SCR-098, SCR-099 and CMP-170/171/172 covering: focus order through the transport and back to the panel region, visible focus on the scrub thumb, the 1 Hz clock live region and its politeness level, `aria-valuetext` wording, the non-colour carrier for coverage shading and for REPLAY state, contrast measurements for the chrome, hit-target sizes, and the keyboard path for every action reachable by pointer (step, seek, bookmark, jump to real time, skip gap).
- A written review record listing each finding with a disposition (fixed in design / accepted / deferred to E26-Q05 with rationale).
- The reduced-motion and high-contrast variants of the REPLAY chrome.

## Out of scope
- The automated axe-core audit of the built screens (E26-Q05).
- Design QA of the built implementation (E26-D08).
- Chart-engine internal motion (E11).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every animation has a reduced-motion answer
  Given the motion spec
  When each specified animation is reviewed
  Then each has an explicit prefers-reduced-motion behaviour
  And no animation's reduced form removes information the user needs

Scenario: The clock does not flood assistive technology
  Given the replay clock updating visually per frame
  When the a11y review examines the live region
  Then the announced region is capped at 1 Hz and uses a polite politeness level
  And the visual readout is decoupled from the announced one

Scenario: Everything reachable by pointer is reachable by keyboard
  Given the SCR-097 interaction inventory
  When the keyboard path is walked
  Then play/pause, step bar, step tick, jump, seek, bookmark, skip gap and jump-to-real-time are all reachable
  And focus never becomes trapped in the scrub control

Scenario: Contrast holds in both themes and in high contrast
  Given the REPLAY chrome in light, dark and high-contrast themes
  Then chrome text meets 4.5:1 and the non-text indicator meets 3:1 in every theme
```

## Technical notes / design
The scrub slider should follow the standard slider keyboard model (arrows step, Home/End jump to range bounds, PageUp/PageDown for coarse movement) while the global replay hotkeys (`<-/->` step bar) apply when focus is outside the slider; this collision must be resolved explicitly in the spec so implementation does not invent a rule.

## Test plan
Review executed against a clickable prototype with a screen reader (NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on macOS) and with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` forced. Findings recorded with severity; blocking findings must be resolved before D07 handoff.

## Security notes
N/A.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility deliverable for the design phase of E26; its record is the evidence cited in the epic DoD's a11y line alongside the E26-Q05 audit.

## Performance notes
The motion spec must be authored against budget #2 — chrome animation is explicitly subordinate to the chart frame budget, and the spec states the suppression threshold rather than leaving it to implementation.

## Observability
N/A.

- [ ] Motion spec merged into `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` motion section (or its replay appendix) and linked here.
- [ ] Accessibility review record published with every finding dispositioned.
- [ ] All blocking findings resolved in the D02/D03/D04/D05 artefacts before handoff.

## Context
The design-ahead rule (`00-planning-brief.md`, `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1) means no frontend replay story may start until its design is Status=Done and has been Done for >=2 sprints. This ticket closes the design track for E26 and transfers it to engineering with everything the implementers need, so that E26-S01 and E26-S02 can enter Ready in Sprint 11 without a single open design question.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A handoff pack covering SCR-097, SCR-098, SCR-099 and CMP-170/171/172: linked Figma frames with redlines, the token inventory used, the state matrix, the full copy deck (including every validation message, the gap message, the speed-limit honesty message, the simulated framing and the not-a-backtest-guarantee caveat), the hotkey table, the motion spec and the a11y review record.

- A list of **design decisions that are load-bearing** and must not be changed without returning to design: the REPLAY chrome treatment, the simulated framing placement, the coverage shading carriers, the 1 Hz clock cap.
- A recorded handoff session with the frontend implementers and the E26 tech lead; open questions raised there are answered in the pack before sign-off.
- The design-QA checklist that E26-D08 will execute, derived from the sign-off checklists in the three screen catalogue entries.

## Out of scope
- New design exploration (D02-D05) and the review itself (D06).

```gherkin

  Given the handoff pack
  When a frontend engineer who did not attend the design work reads it

  And any question they do raise is added to the pack before sign-off

Scenario: Design-ahead is satisfied
  Given the E26 frontend stories are scheduled for Sprint 11 and later
  When this ticket reaches Done
  Then it is Done no later than Sprint 09

Scenario: The design-QA checklist exists before the build starts

```

## Technical notes / design
The state-to-API map must cover at minimum: `created`/`buffering` -> configuring/buffering frames; `playing`/`paused` -> transport states; `finished` -> end-of-range plus the WS `revoked` with `reason: "replay_session_ended"`; `error` -> the error state with `error_message`; client-only `seeking` triggered between issuing a `seek` control call and receiving `snap` frames with `reason: "replay_seek"` on every subscribed topic.

## Test plan
Handoff acceptance is the frontend lead confirming in a comment that the pack is sufficient to open E26-S01 and E26-S02 as Ready.

## Security notes
The copy deck must be reviewed so that no message leaks internal paths, dataset ids or account identifiers to the UI (supports SR-097's "no user-supplied paths" posture by also not surfacing server paths).

## Accessibility notes
The pack carries the a11y review record from D06 and the per-component keyboard tables; implementers must not re-derive them.

## Performance notes
The pack states the perf-relevant design constraints explicitly: 1 Hz announced clock, throttled scrub seek, motion suppression above the stated speed threshold.

## Observability
The pack lists the analytics/audit events each screen emits so instrumentation is not forgotten during implementation.

- [ ] Handoff pack published and linked; handoff session held and recorded.
- [ ] Frontend lead confirms sufficiency in a ticket comment.
- [ ] Design-QA checklist attached to E26-D08.

body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes design QA default-on for net-new UI stories: the built screen is compared against the design spec by a designer and discrepancies are fixed or filed with a priority. E26 ships three net-new screens and three net-new design-system components, and two of its design decisions are safety-relevant (the REPLAY chrome and the simulated framing), so this sweep is not cosmetic.

title: Spike: measure seek cost and hot/cold source throughput at 200-depth symbol-day
body:
## Context
Two numbers decide the shape of the whole replay engine and both are currently assumed rather than measured.

**Seek cost.** `24-internal-schemas.md` §13.7 states seek is bounded at <=2 s for any point in a recorded day, and `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.3 exit criterion #8 tightens the user-visible target to **1 s for a 200-depth symbol**. The algorithm is snapshot anchor (written every `snapshot_interval_s`, default 300 s) -> re-apply deltas to target -> restore `BuilderState` -> warm up metrics. At 200 depth and a busy session, 300 s of orderbook deltas is a large re-apply; the doc itself warns "a seek is never cheaper than a snapshot interval". If the measured cost exceeds budget, the answer is either a shorter snapshot interval (a recorder-side change with a disk cost that E16 owns) or a replay-side checkpoint cache — and that decision must be made before T04 is written, not after.

**Source throughput.** Budget #15 requires sustaining 100x. At 100x, a symbol-day must be read from QuestDB (hot) or Parquet/DuckDB (cold) and merged in `(ts_event, seq)` order fast enough to feed the live pipeline. Whether that needs a prefetching windowed reader, and how large the read-ahead buffer must be to survive a burst period without stalling the clock, is unknown.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Timebox: **4 days**, one backend engineer, agreed with the Architect.
- Measure, against a real recorded BTCUSDT symbol-day at 200 depth produced by the E16 recorder (and one thin-book symbol for contrast):
  1. Snapshot-anchor seek cost at the worst case (target just before the next snapshot), broken down into: anchor load, delta re-apply, `BuilderState` restore, metric warm-up.
  2. The same at snapshot intervals of 300 s, 60 s and 30 s, with the recorder disk cost of each recorded alongside.
  3. Sequential read throughput in events/s from the QuestDB hot tier and from the Parquet/DuckDB cold tier, and the merge cost across streams.
  4. Peak resident memory for a read-ahead buffer sized to 5 s, 30 s and 120 s of replay time at 1x, and the buffer needed to sustain 100x through the busiest minute of the day.
- A comparison table and a recommendation for: snapshot interval, read-ahead strategy (streamed cursor vs prefetched window), tier-selection rule for `source_tier='auto'`, and whether a replay-side checkpoint cache is required.
- **ADR-0018** drafted from the findings (finalised in E26-T07).
- Follow-up tickets filed for whichever path is chosen, including any recorder-side change requested of E16.

## Out of scope
- Production-shippable code. The prototype is explicitly throwaway; the branch is archived unmerged unless the Architect promotes a specific module.
- Frontend work of any kind.
- Optimising the downstream engines — this spike measures the *source and seek*, not footprint or heatmap cost.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The seek budget question is answered with numbers
  Given a 200-depth recorded symbol-day
  When worst-case seek is measured at each candidate snapshot interval
  Then a table of p50/p95/max seek durations with a stage breakdown is recorded
  And a snapshot interval that meets the 1 s p95 target is identified, or the shortfall is quantified with a stated mitigation

Scenario: The 100x question is answered with numbers
  Given the busiest minute of the recorded day
  When the source is read at maximum rate
  Then sustained events/s for both tiers and the read-ahead buffer size needed to avoid a clock stall are recorded

Scenario: A decision is recorded either way
  Given the measurements
  Then ADR-0018 is drafted with the chosen snapshot interval, read-ahead strategy and tier-selection rule
  And follow-up tickets exist for the chosen path, including any E16 recorder change
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the recorded fixture produced by E16 rather than synthetic data — synthetic depth updates do not reproduce the real delta-size distribution that dominates re-apply cost. Instrument the stages separately (`anchor_load_ms`, `delta_apply_ms`, `builder_restore_ms`, `warmup_ms`) because the mitigation differs per stage: a slow anchor load points at storage layout, a slow delta re-apply points at snapshot interval, a slow warm-up points at the metric warm-up window. Measure on the WSL Ubuntu docker-compose target, which is the real deployment shape, not on bare metal.

## Test plan
Benchmark harness only; it is promoted into the CI benchmark suite by E26-Q03 if the Architect approves. Each measurement is run five times and reported as p50/p95/max with the machine spec recorded.

## Security notes
The spike reads recorded data by registry id through the same repository interface production will use — it must not introduce a filesystem-path-taking helper that could later leak into the API surface (SR-097).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI.

## Performance notes
This ticket exists to establish the numbers behind budgets #15 and roadmap exit criterion #8; its output is the baseline that E26-Q03 later enforces in CI.

## Observability
Define the stage-timing metric names here so `replay_seek_duration_ms` can carry a `stage` label consistently from T04 onwards.

- [ ] Questions answered with recorded evidence (tables, machine spec, five runs each).
- [ ] ADR-0018 drafted in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (even if the decision is "defer with mitigation X").

- [ ] Prototype branch archived unmerged or explicitly promoted with normal DoD applying to the promoted part.

title: Add the replay_sessions migration, repository and session lifecycle service
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** The legal state machine (`created -> buffering -> (playing <-> paused) -> finished`, `error` reachable from any state) is the library machine B12 `replay`; the migration/repository stay the bulk of the work, so the estimate is unchanged, but the service layer builds transitions on the factory, not a hand-written table.

> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** The legal state machine (`created -> buffering -> (playing <-> paused) -> finished`, `error` reachable from any state) is the library machine B12 `replay`; the migration/repository stay the bulk of the work, so the estimate is unchanged, but the service layer builds transitions on the factory, not a hand-written table.

> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** The legal state machine (`created -> buffering -> (playing <-> paused) -> finished`, `error` reachable from any state) is the library machine B12 `replay`; the migration/repository stay the bulk of the work, so the estimate is unchanged, but the service layer builds transitions on the factory, not a hand-written table.

A replay session is a server-side object with a lifecycle, not a client-side toy: it is addressed on the WS by id, it holds buffers that must be reclaimed, it survives an app restart so US-RPL-009 can resume it, and it is the unit that paper fills are attributed to. `21-database-schema.md` §3.6.4 specifies the table exactly; this task lands it and the repository/service layer the rest of the epic builds on.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration creating `replay_sessions` exactly per `21-database-schema.md` §3.6.4: columns `id`, `user_id` (FK `users` ON DELETE CASCADE), `recording_session_id` (FK `recording_sessions` ON DELETE SET NULL), `symbol`, `range_start`, `range_end`, `cursor_ts`, `speed numeric(6,2) DEFAULT 1`, `state replay_state DEFAULT 'created'`, `source_tier text DEFAULT 'auto'`, `paper_trading boolean`, `paper_account_id` (FK `exchange_accounts` ON DELETE SET NULL), `bookmarks jsonb DEFAULT '[]'`, `loop_enabled boolean`, `events_emitted bigint`, `gap_warnings integer`, `error_message`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `finished_at`; constraints `rps_range`, `rps_speed` (0.1-100), `rps_tier` (auto|questdb|parquet), `rps_cursor`, `rps_paper`; indexes `ix_rps_user_time` and the partial `ix_rps_live`.
- Confirm the `replay_state` enum (`created|buffering|playing|paused|finished|error`) exists from the base type migration; add it if the base migration did not.
- `ReplaySessionRepository`: create, get-by-id-scoped-to-user, list-by-user with cursor pagination and optional state filter, update state/cursor/counters, soft-finish, delete.
- `ReplaySessionService` lifecycle: `create` (validates the window against coverage and gaps before any buffer is allocated), `transition` (enforces the legal state machine), `reclaim_idle` (2 h idle -> `finished`, buffers freed, per SCR-097's session-expired state), `destroy`.
- A per-user **concurrent-session quota** and a **window-size cap** enforced in the service, both configurable (`CV_REPLAY_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_USER` default 2, `CV_REPLAY_MAX_WINDOW_HOURS` default 24) — the first line of defence against the resource-exhaustion threat.
- Downgrade path tested.
- Implement the `B12` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B12.machine.json`, committed by E50-S01/S02 (hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('replay', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/b12_replay.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_b12_replay.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.

title: Implement ReplaySource: hot/cold readers, ordered k-way merge and gap reporting
body:
## Context
Determinism starts at the read. `24-internal-schemas.md` §13.7 determinism guarantee (1) is that "events replay in `(ts_event, seq)` order, identical to the recorded order" — if the source ever emits out of order, or resolves a tie differently between two runs, every downstream guarantee collapses. The source must also span two storage tiers transparently: QuestDB for hot data and Parquet/DuckDB for cold (`21-database-schema.md` §1, `20-architecture.md` C18), because a window can straddle the roll-off boundary.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `ReplaySource` in `apps/api/.../replay/source.py` exposing an async iterator of recorded events for `(symbols, streams, from, to, depth)`.
- **Hot reader** over QuestDB and **cold reader** over Parquet via DuckDB, behind one interface, both addressed by registry ids and never by caller-supplied paths.
- **Tier selection** implementing `source_tier` `auto|questdb|parquet`: `auto` picks per sub-range using the roll-off boundary, so a window straddling the boundary reads hot for its recent part and cold for its older part, transparently and without duplicating or dropping events at the seam.
- **Ordered k-way merge** across streams (`trades`, `orderbook_delta`, `orderbook_snapshot`, `tickers`, `klines`, `liquidations`, `open_interest`, `funding`) producing a single stream strictly ordered by `(ts_event, seq)`, with a documented, stable tie-break for events sharing both (stream kind ordinal, then recorded insertion order) so two runs can never differ.
- **Read-ahead** per the E26-K01 recommendation: a bounded prefetch buffer with a configurable size (`CV_REPLAY_READAHEAD_EVENTS`), backpressure-aware so a slow consumer stops the read rather than growing memory.
- **Gap reporting**: intersect the window with `recording_gaps` and emit a typed `ReplayGap` marker in-stream at the gap boundary, carrying the gap's start, end and cause, so the clock (T03) and the UI can honour "No data 13:52-13:55 - recorder was offline" rather than silently jumping.
- **Snapshot-anchor lookup** helper used by the seek engine: latest `orderbook_snapshot` at or before a timestamp for a symbol and depth.
- Per-session memory ceiling enforcement with a typed error when exceeded.

## Out of scope
- The clock and pacing (E26-T03) — the source is pull-based and has no notion of speed.
- Seek orchestration (E26-T04) — it consumes the anchor lookup provided here.
- The recorder's write path, retention and coverage endpoint (E16).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Ordering is total and stable
  Given a recorded window containing events that share a ts_event across streams
  When the window is read twice
  Then both reads produce byte-identical event sequences
  And the sequence is non-decreasing in (ts_event, seq)

Scenario: A window straddling the roll-off boundary reads seamlessly
  Given a window whose older half is in Parquet and whose newer half is in QuestDB
  When it is read with source_tier auto
  Then no event is duplicated or dropped at the seam
  And the result equals reading the same window from a single tier holding all of it

Scenario: A gap is reported, never skipped silently
  Given the window intersects a recording_gaps row
  When the source reaches the gap boundary
  Then a ReplayGap marker is emitted carrying its start, end and cause

Scenario: A slow consumer cannot exhaust memory
  Given a consumer that stops reading
  When the read-ahead buffer fills
  Then the source stops reading from storage and resident memory stays flat
  And no events are dropped

Scenario: Paths are never accepted
  When any reader is constructed
  Then the dataset is addressed by registry id and symbol/stream/time, and no filesystem path parameter exists on the public interface
```

## Technical notes / design
Query shapes for both tiers were benchmarked in E07's storage spike ("replay scan of one symbol-day of L2 deltas") and refined in E26-K01; implement against the repository interface established by E07 so a tier swap stays a swap and not a rewrite (ADR-0003).

The merge is a standard heap-based k-way merge over per-stream cursors. The tie-break must be explicit and documented in ADR-0018, because leaving it to the heap's incidental behaviour is exactly how two runs come to differ.

`ReplayGap` is an in-stream control marker, not a market event; downstream the clock consumes it and the injector must never publish it onto a market-data topic.

## Test plan
Unit: merge ordering property test over generated interleavings (Hypothesis); tie-break stability; tier-selection boundary arithmetic; gap intersection including gaps at the exact window edges; memory ceiling error. Integration: read a real recorded fixture from each tier and from a straddling window, asserting sequence equality against a version-controlled expected digest. Perf: sustained events/s recorded against the E26-K01 baseline. Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
SR-097 is the controlling requirement: the public interface accepts no filesystem paths, datasets resolve through the registry, and path-traversal and symlink-escape tests are mandatory on any internal path construction. Reads are bounded by the session's window and the window-size cap from T01, so a crafted request cannot scan the whole lake.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend.

## Performance notes
Must sustain the events/s measured in E26-K01 as the 100x floor for budget #15. Read-ahead sizing follows the K01 recommendation; the buffer is bounded in events and in bytes, whichever binds first.

## Observability
Counter `replay_events_read_total{stream,tier}`, gauge `replay_readahead_events`, counter `replay_gap_warnings_total`, histogram `replay_source_read_seconds{tier}`; the chosen tier per sub-range is logged once per session at info level.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Determinism property tests and the straddling-window integration test green.
- [ ] Tie-break rule documented in ADR-0018 (drafted in E26-K01, finalised in E26-T07).
- [ ] Path-traversal and symlink-escape tests present and green.
- [ ] Throughput benchmark recorded against the K01 baseline; no regression gate wired yet (E26-Q03 does that).
- [ ] Coverage >=85%; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E26-K01` decides the read-ahead strategy and tier-selection rule; `E16-T05` produces the Parquet cold tier this reads.

title: Implement ReplayClock and Injector: pacing, step modes, same-pipeline injection
body:
## Context
This is the heart of principle P2. The `Injector` publishes recorded events on `replay.{session_id}.*` topics **through the same normalizer -> book -> bars -> order-flow chain** as live ingestion (`20-architecture.md` C13), isolated from live state by an env-scoped namespace. The `ReplayClock` is the only thing that differs from live: a monotonic scheduler that emits events preserving inter-event deltas scaled by `speed`.

The most important rule in this ticket is one line from `24-internal-schemas.md` §13.7: **"Backpressure from a slow consumer slows the clock rather than dropping events - replay must never lose data."** US-RPL-002's performance scenario is the user-visible half of the same rule: at high speed on a busy period, "playback keeps up or explicitly reports the achieved rate rather than silently dropping events".

## Scope / Deliverables
- `ReplayClock` in `apps/api/.../replay/clock.py`: monotonic scheduling preserving inter-event deltas scaled by `speed` (0.1-100), with drift correction against a monotonic time source rather than accumulated sleeps.
- **Step mode** (`speed=0`): `step_event`, `step_ms(n)`, `step_bar` — `step_bar` advances until the active `BarSpec` closes a bar, which is what US-RPL-001's "exactly one bar is revealed" and US-RPL-004's arrow-key semantics require.
- **Unbounded mode** (`speed=-1`): emit as fast as consumers accept, for the rule-backtest consumer in E35.
- **Backpressure**: when a consumer cannot keep up, the clock slows and records the achieved rate; it never drops. The achieved-rate figure is exposed on the session so the UI can show it (SCR-097 speed-limit honesty state).
- **Loop support** for US-RPL-008: on reaching a configured loop end, seek back to the loop start and continue, bounded by `loop_enabled` on the session.
- **Gap handling**: on a `ReplayGap` marker, either skip to the gap end (compressing the empty time) or stop at the boundary, per the session's configured behaviour, incrementing `gap_warnings` and surfacing the gap to the client either way.
- `Injector` in `apps/api/.../replay/injector.py`: publishes normalized events onto the bus under a replay-scoped namespace so no replay event can reach live state; sets `source="replay"` on every event; refuses to publish control markers onto market-data topics.
- **Structural isolation**: the OMS must be able to refuse to route replay events to a live account by construction, per determinism guarantee (4) — the `source="replay"` marker is set at injection and is not removable downstream.
- Per-session `asyncio` TaskGroup ownership consistent with `20-architecture.md` §lifecycle ("TaskGroup: replay sessions"), including clean cancellation on session destroy.

## Out of scope
- Seek and state reconstruction (E26-T04).
- REST/WS surfaces (E26-T05).
- Paper matcher behaviour (E38); the `PaperBridge` wiring is E26-S07.
- Any change to the downstream engines — if one proves not replay-safe, a Bug is filed against its owning epic.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Pacing is faithful and drift-free
  Given a recorded window of one hour replayed at 1x
  When playback completes
  Then total elapsed wall-clock time is within 0.5% of one hour
  And no cumulative drift is observable at the end relative to the start

Scenario: Backpressure slows, never drops
  Given a consumer that accepts events at half the required rate at 10x
  When playback runs
  Then every recorded event is still delivered in order
  And the session reports an achieved rate lower than the requested rate

Scenario: Step bar reveals exactly one bar
  Given speed 0 and an active 1-minute BarSpec
  When step_bar is issued once
  Then exactly one bar closes and every dependent view updates consistently

Scenario: Replay events cannot reach live state
  Given a replay session publishing on its namespace
  When the live book engine state for the same symbol is inspected
  Then it is unchanged by the replay traffic
  And every injected event carries source="replay"

Scenario: A gap is honoured explicitly
  Given a ReplayGap marker mid-window and skip-gap configured
  Then the clock jumps to the gap end, increments gap_warnings and notifies the client
  And with stop-at-gap configured it pauses at the boundary instead
```

## Technical notes / design
Scheduling uses a monotonic clock and computes each sleep as `target_wall = session_start_wall + (event_ts - session_start_ts) / speed`, sleeping to the absolute target rather than summing per-event deltas — the latter accumulates drift and would break the 0.5% criterion at long windows.

Speed changes mid-playback rebase `session_start_wall` and `session_start_ts` to the current position so the change takes effect continuously rather than jumping.

The injector's namespace must be part of the bus topic key, not a filter applied after publication, so isolation is structural. Determinism guarantee (4) depends on `source="replay"` being set at injection time and carried on the event object itself.

## Test plan
Unit: pacing math including speed changes mid-playback and drift over a simulated long window; step-mode semantics for each unit; backpressure never drops; loop wrap-around; gap skip and stop. Integration: replay a recorded 10-minute fixture at 1x/4x/25x and assert live state for the same symbol is untouched. Perf: sustained 100x on the K01 fixture without dropped events. Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Isolation is a security control, not only a correctness one: a replay event reaching the OMS as if it were live would be a path to acting on stale prices with real money. The `source="replay"` invariant is tested adversarially in E26-X02. Per-session task ownership guarantees that destroying a session frees its CPU and memory, bounding the resource-exhaustion threat.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. The achieved-rate reporting exists so the UI can be honest about degradation rather than appearing frozen.

## Performance notes
Budget #15: sustain up to 100x crash-free; visual fidelity may degrade but must never desync. Clock lag is the leading indicator and is exported as `replay_clock_lag_ms`.

## Observability
Histogram `replay_clock_lag_ms`, counter `replay_events_emitted_total`, counter `replay_backpressure_seconds_total`, gauge `replay_achieved_speed_ratio`, counter `replay_gap_warnings_total`; a log line per speed change and per gap encountered.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Pacing, step, loop, gap and backpressure tests green; isolation integration test green.
- [ ] 100x sustained run recorded with zero dropped events.
- [ ] `source="replay"` invariant covered by an adversarial test.
- [ ] Coverage >=85%; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E26-T02` supplies the ordered event stream and gap markers; `E26-T01` supplies the session object whose state and counters the clock updates.
