title: Implement SeekEngine: snapshot anchoring, delta re-apply, builder restore
body:
## Context
Scrubbing is the feature users judge replay by, and it is the hardest correctness problem in the epic: after a seek, the book, the in-progress bar, the footprint cells, the profiles and every warmed-up indicator must be exactly what they would have been had the session played from the start. `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.3 exit criterion #8 states it as a hard gate: "scrubbing to an arbitrary timestamp reconstructs correct book, footprint and CVD state within 1 s for a 200-depth symbol".

`24-internal-schemas.md` §13.7 gives the five-step algorithm; this ticket implements it using the parameters measured in E26-K01.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `SeekEngine` in `apps/api/.../replay/` implementing, for a target timestamp:
  1. Find the latest `orderbook_snapshot` at or before the target (written every `snapshot_interval_s` plus on every subscribe and resync) via the T02 anchor lookup.
  2. Load it and rebuild the book to the recorded depth.
  3. Re-apply `orderbook_delta` events from the anchor to the target.
  4. Rebuild bar/footprint/profile state from a persisted `BuilderState` checkpoint (written every 60 s per `(symbol, spec_hash)`) or, absent one, by replaying trades from the enclosing session anchor.
  5. Prime metric warm-up by replaying `max(warmup_bars)` bars of history *before* the target, so indicators are valid at t=0 rather than `None`.
- Emission of a fresh `snap` on every subscribed topic after a seek with `reason: "replay_seek"` (`23-ws-protocol.md` §11), so clients resynchronise rather than infer.
- **Seek cancellation**: a seek superseded by another seek (the user is dragging) is cancelled cleanly without leaking partial state — the scrub drag pattern makes this the common case, not an edge case.
- Seek into or across a gap: land at the nearest valid position on the correct side and report the gap rather than reconstructing from data that does not exist.
- Seek to the exact window start and to the exact window end as explicit cases.
- Optional checkpoint cache if E26-K01 concluded one is required.

## Out of scope
- Changes to bar builders or order-flow engines. `BarBuilder.snapshot()`/`restore()` and the `BuilderState` blob already exist (`24-internal-schemas.md` §4, E12) — this ticket consumes them. Any gap in that contract is a Bug on E12.
- Recorder snapshot cadence (E16 owns it; E26-K01 may have requested a change).
- The frontend scrub interaction (E26-S02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Seek reconstructs exactly
  Given a recorded window played linearly from its start to timestamp X with the derived state captured
  When a fresh session seeks directly to X
  Then the book, in-progress bar, footprint cells, profile levels and CVD equal the linear-play state exactly

Scenario: Seek meets its budget
  Given a 200-depth recorded symbol-day
  When 50 seeks to uniformly random targets are timed
  Then p95 is under 1 s and the maximum is under 2 s

Scenario: Indicators are valid immediately after a seek
  Given an indicator with a 200-bar warm-up requirement
  When the session seeks to X
  Then the indicator has a value at X rather than None

Scenario: A superseded seek leaves no residue
  Given a seek to X in progress
  When a seek to Y is issued before X completes
  Then the session settles at Y with state identical to seeking directly to Y
  And no partial X state is observable

Scenario: Seeking into a gap is explicit
  Given a target inside a recording gap
  When the seek runs
  Then the session lands at the nearest valid timestamp and reports the gap rather than fabricating state
```

## Technical notes / design
Steps 2-3 dominate cost at high depth, which is why the snapshot interval chosen in E26-K01 is load-bearing; instrument each of the five steps separately under `replay_seek_duration_ms{stage=...}` using the stage names defined in K01.

The metric warm-up in step 5 must use the same warm-up path the live pipeline uses on subscribe, or replay and live will disagree on the first bars after a seek — which the determinism harness (T06) will catch, but which is far cheaper to avoid by construction.

Cancellation is implemented by scoping each seek to its own task and awaiting its cancellation before starting the next; state is only swapped into the session atomically at the end of a successful seek, never incrementally.

## Test plan
Unit: anchor selection at boundaries (target exactly on a snapshot, one event after, one before the first snapshot); delta re-apply arithmetic; warm-up bar count; cancellation atomicity. Integration: the linear-play-vs-seek equality test over a real recorded fixture at 20 random targets; gap seek; window-edge seeks. Perf: the 50-seek p95/max benchmark, recorded and later gated by E26-Q03. Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Seek is the most expensive operation a client can trigger and therefore the cheapest denial of service: rate-limit control calls per session, and reject a seek while another is in flight beyond a small queue depth. The target timestamp is validated against the session window (`rps_cursor`), so a client cannot seek outside its own authorised range.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. The <=1 s p95 exists so the UI's seeking state is brief and the announced clock settles quickly.

## Performance notes
Roadmap exit criterion #8 and the SCR-097 note "seek <=1 s to any point within the loaded window" are the binding targets; `24-internal-schemas.md` states the hard ceiling as 2 s. Both are asserted.

## Observability
Histogram `replay_seek_duration_ms{stage}` with stages `anchor_load`, `delta_apply`, `builder_restore`, `warmup`, `total`; counter `replay_seeks_total{result=ok|cancelled|gap|out_of_range}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Linear-play-vs-seek equality test green over a real recorded fixture.
- [ ] p95 <1 s / max <2 s recorded on the 200-depth symbol-day benchmark, or the shortfall escalated with the K01 mitigation applied.
- [ ] Cancellation atomicity test green.
- [ ] Stage metrics emitted with the agreed labels; coverage >=85%; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E26-T03` owns the session's runtime state that seek swaps; `E12` supplies `BarBuilder.snapshot()`/`restore()`, `BuilderState` and the `spec_hash` determinism property (invariant BI-4).

title: Implement the replay REST surface and WS replay_session_id routing
body:
## Context
This task exposes the engine and, more importantly, wires the one hook that makes principle G6 real: subscribing with `replay_session_id` set routes market-data topics from the replay clock instead of the live clock, over the same socket, with the same framing, into the same client rendering path (`23-ws-protocol.md` §11). Everything else in the protocol stays identical — which is precisely the point.

## Scope / Deliverables
- REST, exactly per `22-api-openapi.yaml`:
  - `GET /api/v1/replay/sessions` (cursor pagination, optional `state` filter, `replay:read`, scope self).
  - `POST /api/v1/replay/sessions` (`CreateReplaySessionRequest`; `replay:write`; idempotency recommended, honouring the `Idempotency-Key` and `Idempotency-Replayed` semantics; 201 with `ReplaySession`; **422 `no_data_recorded`** when the window lacks coverage).
  - `GET /api/v1/replay/sessions/{replayId}`, `DELETE /api/v1/replay/sessions/{replayId}` (204, frees buffers).
  - `POST /api/v1/replay/sessions/{replayId}/control` with `ReplayControlRequest` actions `play` (optional `speed`), `pause`, `seek` (`to`), `step` (exactly one of `step_events` or `step_ms`); returns the new `ReplaySession`.
- WS integration (`23-ws-protocol.md` §11):
  - Accept `replay_session_id` on `sub`; route the named market-data topics from that session's clock.
  - Set `source: "replay"` in `snap` metadata and **header flag bit2** on binary frames; carry `rs` (replay session id) in the envelope; add `wt` (wall-clock send time) on replay frames while `ts` remains the **original recorded time**.
  - Emit `snap` with `reason: "replay_seek"` on every subscribed topic after a seek.
  - On reaching `to`: session state `finished`, one `revoked` per topic with `reason: "replay_session_ended"`.
  - **Reject private topics** (`orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet`) subscribed with `replay_session_id` using `invalid_options`.
  - Allow live and replay subscriptions to coexist on one connection, disambiguated by `sub_id`.
  - Error codes `replay_session_not_found` (topic-scoped, `not_found`) and `replay_session_ended` (topic-scoped, `gone`).
- Contract tests generated from the OpenAPI and WS schemas.

## Out of scope
- The engine internals (T02/T03/T04).
- `GET /market/data-coverage` (E16) — consumed only.
- Frontend consumption (E26-S01/S02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Creating a session over uncovered data fails with the documented code
  Given a window with no recorded coverage
  When POST /api/v1/replay/sessions is called
  Then the response is 422 with code no_data_recorded
  And no session row and no buffer are created

Scenario: A replay subscription is marked unmistakably on the wire
  Given a subscription with replay_session_id set
  When frames arrive
  Then snap metadata carries source "replay", binary frames set header flag bit2, the envelope carries rs
  And ts is the original recorded time while wt carries wall-clock send time

Scenario: Private topics are never replayable
  When a sub with replay_session_id names orders, positions, executions or wallet
  Then it is rejected with invalid_options

Scenario: Live and replay coexist on one connection
  Given book.BTCUSDT.200 subscribed live and the same topic subscribed under a replay session
  Then both deliver independently and are disambiguated by sub_id

Scenario: Session end revokes cleanly
  Given playback reaches the end of the window
  Then the session state becomes finished and one revoked frame per topic is emitted with reason replay_session_ended

Scenario: Another user's session is invisible
  Given a session owned by user A
  When user B references it on REST or on a sub
  Then REST returns not-found and the sub is rejected with replay_session_not_found
```

## Technical notes / design
`step` carries exactly one of `step_events` or `step_ms`; enforce the exclusivity in the request model and return 422 with a field-level message otherwise. `seek` repositions `cursor_ts` and is never cheaper than a snapshot interval — the API doc says so, and the control response returns the session so the client can render the seeking state from real state rather than optimistically.

Control-call rate limiting lives here rather than in the engine, so a scrub drag that fires many seeks is coalesced at the edge: apply a short debounce window per session and treat the latest target as authoritative.

## Test plan
Contract: OpenAPI request/response validation for every operation and error; WS schema conformance for `sub` with `replay_session_id`, `snap` `reason` values, `revoked` reasons and the error registry entries. Integration: full lifecycle create -> subscribe -> play -> seek -> step -> end -> revoked against a recorded fixture. Security: cross-user access, private-topic rejection, control-call rate limit. Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
`replay:read`/`replay:write`, scope `self`. Cross-user references return not-found rather than forbidden. No filesystem path is accepted by any operation (SR-097) — windows are addressed by symbol and time only. Control endpoints are rate-limited per session and per user to bound the seek-amplification denial of service. Idempotency on create prevents a retried request from allocating a second session and a second buffer.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. The control response returning authoritative state is what lets the UI announce the settled position rather than a predicted one.

## Performance notes
Budget #3 (WS tick to screen p95 <100 ms) still applies to replay frames measured via `wt`, which exists precisely so latency instrumentation keeps working when `ts` is recorded time.

## Observability
Counters `replay_control_calls_total{action,result}`, `replay_subscriptions_total`; the replay-session-start OpenTelemetry span (one of the two traced paths in `20-architecture.md` §observability) is started here and carries session id, symbol, window length and tier.

## Definition of Done

title: Build the replay determinism and live-parity harness as a required CI check
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §6.3 exit criterion #1 is not a claim to be made in a demo, it is a test: "All order-flow views render from a single shared pipeline used identically by live and replay - **verified by a test that replays a recorded day and asserts view state equals the state captured live**". Criterion #7 adds detector reproducibility and criterion #8 adds cross-run determinism. §6.4 lists "Determinism | Replay double-run equality test; detector event-stream equality test" as a quality gate.

This harness is the single most valuable artefact in the epic: it is what converts "replay is the same code path" from an architectural intention into an enforced property, and it is what R3 relies on when it uses replay as a trading-logic test bed.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A **capture mode** in the recorder-adjacent test tooling that, while a fixture is recorded live (or from the synthetic feed), also captures the derived state at checkpoints: bars per active `BarSpec`, footprint cells, profile levels, CVD, Deep-Stats values and every `deterministic=True` metric, with their `spec_hash`.
- A **live-parity test**: replay the recorded fixture and diff every captured derived value against the replayed value. Tolerance 0 for exact metrics, 1e-9 for floats (`24-internal-schemas.md` §metric descriptors). Any difference fails CI with a diff report naming the first divergent timestamp, stream and field — a bare boolean failure would be useless at this scale.
- A **double-run equality test**: replay the same window twice in the same run and assert byte-identical emitted event streams and derived series; plus a cross-machine assertion by comparing against a version-controlled digest so a developer machine and CI must agree.
- A **detector event-stream equality test** (criterion #7): replaying the same recorded window twice yields identical detector events, including their inputs and threshold values.
- A **seek-parity test** delegating to E26-T04's linear-play-vs-seek equality assertion so it runs in the same gate.
- Version-controlled golden fixtures in `packages/fixtures`: one normal session, one high-volatility burst, one containing a WS disconnect and resync, one with a sequence gap, one thin-book symbol (the §6.4 integration fixture list).
- Wire the suite as a **required CI check** on `main`, with a documented procedure for regenerating goldens that requires a reviewer from both the engine and QA sides.

## Out of scope
- Fixing divergences found in downstream engines — those are Bugs filed against E18/E19/E20/E21/E23/E25.
- The offline DuckDB recomputation parity check (§6.3 criterion #6) — that is owned by the order-flow epics; this harness may reuse its fixtures.
- Performance benchmarking (E26-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Live parity is enforced, not asserted
  Given a recorded fixture with derived state captured live
  When the harness replays it in CI
  Then every derived value matches within tolerance
  And any mismatch fails the build with the first divergent timestamp, stream and field named

Scenario: Double-run equality holds across machines
  Given the same window replayed on CI and on a developer machine
  Then both produce identical event streams and derived series
  And both match the version-controlled digest

Scenario: Detector events are reproducible
  Given a window containing iceberg and stop-run detector firings
  When it is replayed twice
  Then the detector event streams are identical including inputs and thresholds

Scenario: Goldens cannot drift silently
  When a golden fixture or digest is regenerated
  Then the change requires review from both an engine owner and QA
  And the PR states why the expected values changed
```

## Technical notes / design
Checkpoint at bar closes rather than per event: per-event capture would be enormous and would mostly re-assert the same property. Capture per `(symbol, spec_hash)` so a builder-config change is visible as a fixture mismatch rather than as a silent pass.

The diff report should be structured (first divergence plus a bounded context window), because a full diff of a symbol-day is unreadable and unreadable output is how a failing determinism gate becomes a disabled determinism gate.

Run the full symbol-day suite nightly and a reduced one-hour suite on every PR, so the gate is enforced on every change without making PR CI unusable.

## Test plan
The harness *is* the test plan; its own unit tests cover the diff reporter, the tolerance logic and the fixture loader. A deliberate mutation test proves the harness fails when the pipeline is perturbed: inject a one-tick offset into a bar builder behind a test flag and assert the harness catches it.

## Security notes
Fixtures are recorded market data only (classification A-10) with no account identifiers, keys or PII. Fixture integrity matters: a corrupted golden silently weakens the gate, so fixtures carry a checksum manifest verified on read, mirroring SR-094's posture for the Parquet archive.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
The PR-tier suite must complete within the CI budget agreed with DevSecOps; the nightly tier carries the full symbol-day. Report harness runtime so it does not silently grow into a bottleneck.

## Observability
Publish the pass/fail and the first-divergence summary as a CI artefact; track the suite's runtime as a metric so regressions in the harness itself are visible.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Live-parity, double-run, detector-equality and seek-parity tests implemented and green.
- [ ] Five golden fixtures committed with a checksum manifest and a documented regeneration procedure requiring dual review.
- [ ] Suite wired as a required check on `main` (PR tier) plus a nightly full tier.
- [ ] Mutation test proves the harness actually fails on a perturbed pipeline.
- [ ] Roadmap exit criteria #1, #7 and #8 each map to a named test in this suite, documented on the ticket.

## Dependencies
`E26-T03` must be able to replay a window; `E18` and `E23` supply the footprint and CVD state the parity test diffs (profiles, Deep-Stats and detectors are added as their epics land, without changing this harness's structure).

## Branch

title: Finalise ADR-0018, replay observability and plan-doc reconciliation
body:
## Context
Two things close out the engine track. First, the decisions taken in E26-K01 and implemented across T02-T05 must be recorded as an ADR, because the snapshot interval, the merge tie-break and the resource-governance limits are exactly the kind of choice a future maintainer will otherwise reverse by accident. Second, several plan documents will have drifted from shipped behaviour during implementation — and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` requires docs to reflect *final shipped behaviour, not the original proposal*.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **ADR-0018 "Replay determinism, seek strategy and resource governance"** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`, covering: the one-code-path injection design and why a parallel replay implementation was rejected; the `(ts_event, seq)` ordering rule and the documented tie-break; the snapshot interval chosen in E26-K01 with its disk cost; the read-ahead and tier-selection strategy; the backpressure-slows-the-clock rule; the resource-governance limits (sessions per user, window cap, memory ceiling, idle reclaim, control-call rate limit); and the consequences of each.
- **Observability completion**: register the full metric set (`replay_sessions_active`, `replay_events_emitted_total`, `replay_clock_lag_ms`, `replay_seek_duration_ms{stage}`, `replay_source_tier`, `replay_gap_warnings_total`, `replay_backpressure_seconds_total`, `replay_session_memory_bytes`, `replay_achieved_speed_ratio`), add a Grafana dashboard for replay health, and add alert rules for sustained clock lag, repeated seek-budget breaches and session-reclaim storms, per `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0014-observability.md`.
- **Plan-doc reconciliation**:
  - `15-component-catalogue.md` — the CMP-171 speed-preset list resolved in E26-D01 versus the SCR-097 list; CMP-170 coverage-shading prop added.
  - `14-screens-catalogue.md` — any SCR-097/098/099 state added or renamed during implementation; the SCR-097 "speed 0.25x-50x" phrasing in the sign-off checklist reconciled with the API's documented 0.1-100 range and the shipped preset list.
  - `24-internal-schemas.md` §13.7 — the seek algorithm parameters as shipped.
  - `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` §11 — any field or error added during T05.
  - `20-architecture.md` C13 — module boundaries as built.
- A changelog fragment for the replay feature per `07-release-and-prr.md`.

## Out of scope
- New engineering behaviour — this task documents and instruments what exists; a needed behaviour change is a separate ticket.
- ADRs owned by other epics (ADR-0015 recording policy, ADR-0003 storage tiers) beyond cross-references.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The ADR records decisions with their evidence
  Given ADR-0018
  When it is reviewed by the Architect
  Then each decision cites the E26-K01 measurement or the implementation constraint that drove it
  And the rejected alternatives are stated with the reason for rejection

Scenario: Docs match shipped behaviour
  Given the shipped replay feature
  When the listed plan documents are diffed against it
  Then every divergence is corrected, and the speed-preset discrepancy between SCR-097 and CMP-171 is resolved to one canonical list everywhere

Scenario: Replay health is observable before it is needed
  Given the Grafana dashboard and alert rules
  When clock lag is sustained above threshold in a soak run
  Then an alert fires and the dashboard shows the responsible stage
```

## Technical notes / design
The alert thresholds should be derived from the E26-K01 and E26-Q03 measurements rather than guessed: sustained `replay_clock_lag_ms` above the level at which the achieved rate diverges from the requested rate, and `replay_seek_duration_ms{stage=total}` p95 above the 1 s budget over a rolling window.

## Test plan
Doc review by the Architect and the CDO track for the catalogue changes; dashboard and alert rules validated by firing them deliberately in a soak run (coordinated with E26-Q03).

## Security notes
The ADR must record the security-relevant decisions explicitly — SR-097 registry-id addressing, private topics never replayable, `source="replay"` isolation, and the resource-governance limits — so they are not later relaxed as "just limits". Reviewed alongside E26-X03.

## Accessibility notes
Catalogue reconciliation must preserve the a11y requirements recorded on SCR-097/098/099 and CMP-170/171/172; any change to them requires the accessibility specialist's agreement.

## Performance notes
The dashboard is the standing evidence for budgets #2 and #15 after the epic closes.

## Observability
This ticket *is* the observability deliverable for E26.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] ADR-0018 merged and referenced from `27-adrs/README.md`.
- [ ] All listed plan documents reconciled; the speed-preset discrepancy resolved to one canonical list.
- [ ] Metric set registered, dashboard committed, alert rules deployed and deliberately fired once.
- [ ] Changelog fragment merged.
- [ ] Architect sign-off recorded.

`E26-T06` and `E26-T05` must be complete so the ADR documents what shipped; `E26-D01` supplies the speed-preset decision.

title: Create a replay session from SCR-098 with coverage-aware range selection
body:
## Context
Implements **US-RPL-001** (bar-by-bar replay, Must — its "before available history" scenario in particular) and the setup half of **US-RPL-009**. SCR-098 is where the recorder-dependency becomes concrete: a session can only exist over a window the recorder covered, and `14-screens-catalogue.md` §global rule 3 requires that limit to be a designed, explanatory state rather than an error.

Design is E26-D03, Done in Sprint 08, satisfying the design-ahead rule.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Build **SCR-098 Replay session setup modal** per the E26-D07 handoff pack, composed from CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-219 SymbolPicker, CMP-172 ReplayRangePicker, CMP-047 DatePicker/DateRangePicker, CMP-171 ReplaySpeedPicker, CMP-026 EmptyState, CMP-027 ErrorState.
- Implement **CMP-172 ReplayRangePicker** as a design-system component per its E26-D05 spec: `symbol`, `availableRanges: {from,to}[]`, `onSelectRange`, with recorder-availability shading so only recorded ranges are selectable, and the Default / PartialAvailability / NoRecordedHistory(EmptyState) Storybook variants.
- Implement **CMP-171 ReplaySpeedPicker** with the canonical preset list plus the custom-value affordance (US-RPL-004 "plus a custom value").
- Fetch coverage from `GET /api/v1/market/data-coverage?symbol` and render recorded / partial / missing windows on the range track with a text alternative.
- Create the session via `POST /api/v1/replay/sessions` with `{ symbols, from, to, speed, streams, depth, paper_account_id, autostart }`, sending an `Idempotency-Key`.
- Client-side validation mirroring the server contract with human-language messages: range end after start; range must intersect coverage ("Nothing is recorded for that window."); speed within 0.1-100; paper trading requires a paper account. Pre-empt the server's 422 `no_data_recorded` rather than surfacing it raw.
- **Start-before-history offer** (US-RPL-001 scenario 3): when the chosen start precedes available data, offer the earliest available timestamp with the reason stated and accept it in one action.
- **Resume** (US-RPL-009): surface an existing saved session for the symbol with its timestamp and speed alongside "Start fresh", and the data-changed variant offering the nearest available start when the underlying data was pruned.
- Preparation progress with the estimate shown before starting for large requests, and a cancel action.
- Entry points: the `/replay` route's empty state and the "open in replay" actions from the journal (SCR-094) and the footprint cell context menu, passing symbol and timestamp as prefill.

## Out of scope
- The replay page itself and playback (E26-S02).
- Paper-trading results (E26-S07).
- `GET /market/data-coverage` implementation (E16).
- Multi-symbol sessions beyond passing the array through — multi-pane behaviour is E26-S05.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Only recorded ranges can be chosen
  Given a symbol recorded from 2026-09-01 with a gap on 2026-09-05
  When the range picker renders
  Then unrecorded windows are not selectable and are distinguishable without relying on colour
  And the available ranges are also listed as text

Scenario: A start before available history becomes an offer, not a rejection
  Given the user picks a start earlier than the earliest recorded timestamp
  When they attempt to continue
  Then the earliest available timestamp is offered with the reason stated
  And accepting it takes one action and proceeds to session creation

Scenario: An uncovered window is refused in the client, with help
  Given a range intersecting no recorded coverage
  When the user attempts to create the session
  Then the modal states that nothing is recorded for that window and names the nearest recorded range
  And no request is sent

Scenario: A pruned saved session is explained on resume
  Given a saved replay position whose data has since been pruned
  When the modal opens for that symbol
  Then it states what changed and offers the nearest available start point
  And Start fresh clears the saved state for that symbol

Scenario: Preparation states its cost
  Given a three-symbol full-day request
  When the user submits
  Then the estimated preparation time is shown before preparation begins and a cancel control is available throughout

Scenario: A retried submission does not create two sessions
  Given a network retry of the create request with the same Idempotency-Key
  Then the original session is returned and only one session exists
```

## Technical notes / design
Server constraints to mirror client-side with friendly copy (`21-database-schema.md` §3.6.4): `rps_range`, `rps_speed` (0.1-100), `rps_paper` (paper requires an account). The paper-account selector lists only accounts the caller has been granted. Coverage is fetched once per symbol selection and cached for the modal's lifetime; the range control must not refetch per drag frame.

Prefill from external entry points sets symbol and centres the range on the passed timestamp with a sensible default window, then still validates against coverage.

## Test plan
Unit: validation rules, the earliest-available offer, preset and custom speed handling, coverage-to-track mapping including gaps at window edges. Component: CMP-171 and CMP-172 Storybook variants with unit, visual, axe and keyboard tests per their catalogue entries. Integration: session creation against a stubbed API including the 422 `no_data_recorded` path and the idempotent retry. E2E: covered in E26-Q02. Coverage >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
No filesystem path is ever entered or displayed (SR-097). The paper-account list is scoped to granted accounts. A session id belonging to another user is not resolvable — the resume path must handle a not-found gracefully rather than exposing existence. Data classification: recorded market data (A-10), plus account references.

## Accessibility notes
Labelled form controls for range, symbol multiselect, speed and paper account; the available-history statement is adjacent text rather than a tooltip; validation errors name their field and are wired via `aria-describedby`; the coverage timeline has a text alternative listing recorded ranges; the modal traps focus correctly and restores it on close. axe-core green; manual screen-reader spot-check on the range picker.

## Performance notes
SCR-098 budget: a 1-day single-symbol session is ready in <=10 s with progress shown; larger requests state the estimated preparation time before starting. Coverage fetch is cached per symbol for the modal's lifetime.

## Observability
`replay.session_created {range, symbols, speed}` analytics on success; `replay.session_deleted` where the modal offers deletion of a stale session.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by automated tests or by a recorded manual QA step with a follow-up automation task.
- [ ] CMP-171 and CMP-172 published to Storybook with their catalogue-specified test set.
- [ ] Coverage >=80% on the touched frontend package.
- [ ] axe-core green on SCR-098; keyboard-only path verified; manual screen-reader spot-check recorded.

- [ ] QA sign-off recorded; demoed at Sprint Review; feature-flag state recorded (`replay.enabled`, default on in staging).
- [ ] PRs merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E26-T05` supplies the create endpoint and its error contract; `E26-D07` is the signed-off design handoff (design-ahead satisfied: E26-D03 Done in Sprint 08).

title: Build SCR-097 replay page: transport, scrubbing and unmistakable REPLAY chrome
body:
## Context
Implements **US-RPL-001** (bar-by-bar replay, Must) and **US-RPL-004** (playback controls, Must) — the two Must stories that define the epic's user-visible core. SCR-097 hosts the same dockable panel set as the terminal, fed by the replay clock: the panels themselves are unchanged, which is the visible proof of principle G6 that replay and live share one rendering path.

The safety requirement is explicit in the SCR-097 sign-off: "REPLAY chrome cannot be confused with live". A trader who mistakes replay for live can act on prices from hours ago.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Build the **`/replay` route and SCR-097 page**: header line (`REPLAY  <SYMBOL>  <timestamp to ms>  speed Nx`), the dockable panel region reusing the terminal's panel host (CMP-180 ChartRoot, CMP-196 MultiChartLinker), the transport row, the speed picker, the scrub track and the option row.
- Implement **CMP-170 ReplayScrubber** as a design-system component per E26-D05: props `currentTime`, `range`, `speed`, `playing`, `bookmarks?`, `onPlayPause`, `onSpeedChange`, `onScrub`, `onStepBar`, `onStepTick`, `onJumpToRealtime`, plus the coverage-shading extension; Storybook variants Paused, Playing, HighSpeed, WithBookmarks, KeyboardControlDemo, Seeking, GapAhead, EndOfRange, SessionExpired.
- Subscribe to the market-data topics (`trades.{symbol}`, `book.{symbol}.{depth}`, `bars.…`, `footprint.…`) with `replay_session_id` set, and render the frames through the *existing* panel implementations — no replay-specific rendering path.
- Drive playback via `POST /api/v1/replay/sessions/{replayId}/control` with `play` / `pause` / `seek` / `step`, treating the returned session as authoritative state.
- **Hotkeys** per SCR-097: `Space` play/pause, `<-/->` step one bar, `Shift+<-/->` step one tick, `Ctrl+<-/->` jump one minute, `R` jump to real time (exits replay after confirm), `B` set bookmark, `[`/`]` previous/next bookmark, drag the scrubber to seek. Register them in the Replay context group of the SCR-030 hotkey overlay.
- **REPLAY chrome**: the purple border variant, the clock and a badge on every replaying pane, per the E26-D02 spec, with the reduced-motion and high-contrast variants from E26-D06.
- All SCR-097 states: configuring, buffering, playing, paused, seeking, **gap encountered** ("No data 13:52-13:55 - recorder was offline. [Skip gap] [Stop here]"), end of range, paper-fill mode active, **session expired** (2 h idle reclaim, with resume).
- **Speed-limit honesty**: when the engine reports an achieved rate below the requested rate, show the achieved rate rather than appearing to keep up; disable paper fills above 25x with the reason stated.
- Handle WS `snap` with `reason: "replay_seek"` by resynchronising every pane, and `revoked` with `reason: "replay_session_ended"` by entering the end-of-range state.

## Out of scope
- Tick-level stepping semantics beyond wiring the key (E26-S03).
- Book/heatmap replay specifics (E26-S04), multi-pane sync (E26-S05), navigation aids and bookmarks persistence (E26-S06), paper trading (E26-S07), session restore (E26-S08).
- Any change to the order-flow panels themselves.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Starting a replay rewinds and hides the future
  Given a session created over 13:00-15:00 starting at 13:00
  When the page loads the session
  Then the chart shows data up to 13:00 and no future bars are visible
  And the REPLAY chrome, clock and per-pane badges are present

Scenario: Stepping reveals exactly one bar consistently
  When the step-bar key is pressed
  Then exactly one bar is revealed
  And every dependent view (footprint, delta, stats, CVD) updates to the same timestamp

Scenario: Scrubbing resynchronises every pane
  When the user drags the scrubber to an arbitrary time and releases
  Then a seek is issued, each pane receives a fresh snapshot with reason replay_seek
  And all panes show the same timestamp within the 1 s p95 budget

Scenario: Replay is never mistaken for live
  Given the page is in any playback state
  Then the REPLAY chrome and clock are visible and conveyed by text, not colour alone
  And pressing R requires a confirmation before leaving replay for real time

Scenario: A gap is surfaced, with a choice
  Given playback reaches a recorder gap
  Then playback halts at the boundary and names the exact missing range
  And Skip gap and Stop here are both available and keyboard-reachable

Scenario: The engine is honest when it cannot keep up
  Given 100x is requested on a busy period and the backend reports a lower achieved rate
  Then the achieved rate is displayed
  And no events are silently missing from any pane

Scenario: An expired session offers resumption rather than failing
  Given the server reclaimed the session after 2 h idle
  Then the session-expired state is shown with a resume action
  And resuming recreates the session at the last cursor position
```

## Technical notes / design
`state` from the API maps to the visual states (`created`/`buffering` -> buffering, `playing`, `paused`, `finished` -> end of range, `error`); `seeking` is a client-only condition between issuing a `seek` and receiving the `replay_seek` snapshots. The control response is authoritative — never optimistically advance the clock past what the server reports, or the displayed timestamp will lie during backpressure.

Scrub drag issues at most one seek per settle (debounced), matching the server-side coalescing in E26-T05; intermediate drag positions update the thumb locally without requesting a seek.

The clock's visual readout may update per frame; the **announced** live region is capped at 1 Hz per the a11y spec — these are two separate elements, as specified in E26-D06.

Frames carry `source: "replay"` and `rs`; the client must assert that every frame rendered on this page carries them and must refuse to render a frame that does not, rather than trusting page context.

## Test plan
Unit: state mapping, hotkey dispatch including focus-dependent arrow-key resolution inside versus outside the slider, debounce logic, achieved-rate display, frame-provenance assertion. Component: CMP-170 Storybook variants with unit, visual, axe, keyboard and scrub-responsiveness tests per its catalogue entry. Integration: full lifecycle against a stubbed WS/REST including seek, gap, end-of-range and expiry. E2E and perf: E26-Q02 and E26-Q03. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
The page must never render a frame lacking the replay provenance markers — this is the client half of the isolation invariant and is probed adversarially in E26-X02. No account identifiers appear in the replay chrome. Jump-to-real-time requires confirmation so a user cannot leave replay into a live surface by a single accidental keystroke.

## Accessibility notes
The replay clock is a labelled live region updated at most 1 Hz; the scrubber is `role="slider"` with `aria-valuetext` in absolute human-readable time; transport controls are labelled buttons carrying shortcut hints; visible focus throughout; the gap state's actions are keyboard-reachable; REPLAY state is conveyed by text and shape, not colour alone; reduced-motion behaviour per E26-D06. axe-core green plus a manual screen-reader pass.

## Performance notes
Budget #2: p95 frame time <=16.6 ms and never below 30 fps with the full order-flow scene, worst case explicitly including replay at 20x. SCR-097: sustain 25x on 1-minute data and 4x on raw tick data without dropping frames; seek <=1 s within the loaded window. Chrome motion is suppressed above the threshold set in E26-D06 so frame budget is spent on the chart.

## Observability
`replay.started`, `replay.seek` analytics; client-side frame-budget telemetry tagged with the replay speed so the perf suite can attribute regressions.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by automated tests or a recorded manual QA step with an automation follow-up.
- [ ] CMP-170 published to Storybook with its full catalogue test set including the keyboard table.
- [ ] Coverage >=80%; axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass recorded; keyboard-only path verified.
- [ ] perf: budget #2 measured with the full order-flow scene under replay at 20x and recorded; seek p95 recorded.
- [ ] design-qa: two-second replay-identification check passed on the build (also re-verified in E26-D08).
- [ ] QA sign-off; demoed at Sprint Review; feature-flag state recorded.
- [ ] PRs merged via the merge queue (split along page / component / hotkeys to stay within the 400 LOC guidance).

## Dependencies
`E26-S01` creates the session this page consumes; `E26-T05` supplies control and WS routing; `E26-D07` is the signed-off handoff.

title: Tick-by-tick replay with honest rate reporting and a no-tick-data fallback
body:
## Context
Implements **US-RPL-002** (tick-by-tick replay, Should). Tick stepping is what makes replay an order-flow tool rather than a chart toy: stepping one print at a time and watching footprint, delta, tape, CVD and the stats rows move together is how a trader reconstructs *how* a move developed. The story's NFR is the determinism guarantee enforced by E26-T06.

Two honesty requirements come from the story itself: a range with only bar data must **disable tick replay with an explanation and offer bar replay** rather than pretending, and at high speed the system must **report the achieved rate rather than silently dropping events**.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Wire `Shift+<-/->` and the transport's step-tick controls to `POST /api/v1/replay/sessions/{replayId}/control` with `{ action: "step", step_events: 1 }`, and a configurable step size for stepping several prints at once.
- Ensure a tick step propagates to every dependent view in one consistent update: footprint cells, per-bar delta, the tape, CVD and the Deep-Stats rows all reflect exactly the prints applied — no view may lag by one event.
- **Tick availability detection**: derive from the session's `streams` and the coverage response whether raw `trades` are available for the window. When only bar/kline data exists, disable tick controls with an explanation and offer bar replay as the alternative in the same message.
- **Achieved-rate reporting** at high speeds: surface the backend's achieved rate in the transport when it diverges from the requested rate, with an explanatory tooltip, rather than allowing the UI to imply the requested rate is being met.
- The mixed case: a window whose earlier part has ticks and whose later part is bars-only must degrade at the boundary with a stated reason rather than failing the whole session.

## Out of scope
- The backend step semantics (E26-T03) and the control endpoint (E26-T05).
- Book and heatmap reconstruction during tick stepping (E26-S04).
- Determinism verification (E26-T06).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One print, every view
  Given a replay paused mid-bar with footprint, delta, tape, CVD and stats rows visible
  When the step-tick control is used once
  Then exactly one print is applied
  And footprint, delta, tape, CVD and the stats rows all reflect that print in the same update

Scenario: No tick data is explained, not hidden
  Given a window for which only bar data was recorded
  When the replay page loads
  Then tick replay controls are disabled with an explanation
  And bar replay is offered in the same message

Scenario: High speed reports the truth
  Given replay at 100x over a busy period where the engine achieves 60x
  Then the transport shows the achieved rate
  And every recorded event is still applied in order, with none skipped

Scenario: A mid-window fidelity change degrades gracefully
  Given ticks are available until 14:00 and only bars afterwards
  When playback crosses 14:00
  Then tick controls become unavailable with the reason stated and playback continues in bar mode
```

## Technical notes / design
The step control is issued server-side rather than simulated client-side, so the same code path advances state whether the user steps or plays — stepping must not become a second implementation.

Achieved rate comes from the session payload (`replay_achieved_speed_ratio` surfaced on the session object by E26-T03/T05); the UI thresholds display so that trivial jitter does not flicker the readout, but any sustained divergence is shown.

## Test plan
Unit: availability derivation from `streams` and coverage, the disabled-with-explanation state, rate-display thresholding, step-size handling. Integration: step once against a fixture and assert every dependent view advanced by exactly one print (this is a strong regression guard against a view being fed from a second path). E2E in E26-Q02. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
Step calls are rate-limited server-side; the client must not allow key-repeat to generate an unbounded control-call storm — hold-to-repeat is throttled.

## Accessibility notes
Step controls are labelled buttons with shortcut hints; `Shift+<-/->` is documented in the hotkey overlay; the disabled-with-explanation state associates its reason with the control via `aria-describedby` rather than relying on a tooltip; the achieved-rate change is announced politely, not assertively.

## Performance notes
Budget #15 covers the 100x case; SCR-097 requires 4x on raw tick data without dropped frames. Held key-repeat stepping must not exceed one in-flight control call at a time.

## Observability
Analytics on step usage frequency and on the achieved-rate divergence event, so the perf team learns which windows and speeds actually degrade in practice.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios automated or covered by a recorded manual step with an automation follow-up.
- [ ] The one-step-one-print integration test green across all dependent views.
- [ ] Coverage >=80%; axe-core green; keyboard path verified.
- [ ] QA sign-off; demoed; feature-flag state recorded; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E26-S02` supplies the page, transport and hotkey plumbing.

title: Replay the order book and liquidity heatmap with a not-recorded state
body:
## Context
Implements **US-RPL-003** (order-book replay, Should). Liquidity context is half of order-flow analysis: without the ladder and the heatmap, a replayed move shows what traded but not what was sitting there. The story's NFR names the mechanism — "periodic snapshots written by the recorder to bound seek time" — which is exactly the anchor the seek engine uses.

The honesty requirement is sharp: when only trades were recorded for a period, **DOM and heatmap show an explicit "not recorded" state while price and footprint still replay**. Partial fidelity must be visible, not inferred from an empty-looking ladder.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Subscribe `book.{symbol}.{depth}` with `replay_session_id` set so the E21 DOM ladder and liquidity heatmap render from replayed snapshots and deltas through their existing implementations.
- Rebuild on seek: consume the `snap` frames with `reason: "replay_seek"` for the book topic and reset the heatmap's rolling texture history to the reconstructed window rather than retaining pre-seek columns.
- **"Not recorded" state** for DOM and heatmap when `orderbook_delta` / `orderbook_snapshot` streams are absent for the window or for a sub-range, while price, trades and footprint continue replaying — implemented with the existing recorder-dependent emptiness pattern (CMP-026 EmptyState) rather than a new one.
- Depth honesty: when the session was created at a lower depth than the panel is configured for, state the actual replayed depth rather than rendering a shallower book as if it were complete.
- Heatmap time-axis alignment with the replay clock, so the heatmap's newest column corresponds to the replay timestamp and not to wall-clock time.
- Handle the mid-window transition where book data starts or stops (recorder gap in the book streams only).

## Out of scope
- The DOM ladder and heatmap implementations themselves (E21) — consumed unchanged; any replay-incompatibility found is a Bug on E21.
- Seek reconstruction internals (E26-T04).
- Recorder snapshot cadence (E16).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Book and heatmap reconstruct at the replay timestamp
  Given a session with orderbook streams recorded
  When playback reaches a timestamp
  Then the DOM ladder and heatmap show the book as recorded at that timestamp
  And the heatmap's newest column corresponds to the replay clock, not wall-clock time

Scenario: Seeking rebuilds the book within budget
  When the user seeks to an arbitrary time
  Then the book rebuilds from the nearest prior snapshot
  And it is correct and visible within 2 seconds

Scenario: Missing book data is stated, and does not stop the rest
  Given a period for which only trades were recorded
  Then the DOM ladder and heatmap show an explicit not-recorded state naming the affected range
  And price and footprint continue to replay normally

Scenario: Replayed depth is not overstated
  Given the session was created at depth 50 while the panel is configured for 200
  Then the panel states the actual replayed depth rather than implying full depth

Scenario: Stale columns never survive a seek
  Given the heatmap has accumulated history before a seek
  When the seek completes
  Then no pre-seek column remains visible
```

## Technical notes / design
The heatmap's rolling texture is a ring buffer keyed by time; on `replay_seek` it must be cleared and repopulated from the reconstructed window rather than continuing to append, otherwise columns from two different times sit side by side — a subtle and highly misleading bug class, which is why it has its own acceptance scenario.

Depth comes from the session's `depth` field; the panel reads it from the session rather than assuming its own configured value.

## Test plan
Unit: not-recorded state derivation per sub-range, depth reconciliation, ring-buffer reset on seek. Integration: replay a fixture containing a book-stream gap and assert the ladder and heatmap enter and leave the not-recorded state at the right timestamps while footprint continues. Parity: the book state at checkpoints is part of the E26-T06 harness. E2E in E26-Q02. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
No new data exposure — replayed book data is the user's own recorded data, addressed by symbol and time (SR-097). Depth is bounded by the session's recorded depth, so a client cannot request deeper replay than was recorded.

## Accessibility notes
The not-recorded state is text, reachable in the DOM mirror, and names the affected range; the heatmap retains its non-colour alternative (numeric depth inspection) under replay exactly as under live, per the R2 a11y gate.

## Performance notes
Budget #14's heatmap cadence applies to live; under replay the binding constraint is that the reconstruction and the rolling upload keep budget #2's frame floor at up to 20x. Measured in E26-Q03.

## Observability
Count entries into the not-recorded state by symbol and range so the recorder's coverage weaknesses become visible in practice rather than anecdotally.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios automated or covered by a recorded manual step with follow-up.
- [ ] Book state included in the E26-T06 parity checkpoints.
- [ ] Coverage >=80%; axe-core green; not-recorded state screen-reader verified.
- [ ] perf: 20x replay with the ladder and heatmap open measured against budget #2.
- [ ] QA sign-off; demoed; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E26-S03` establishes tick-level replay behaviour this builds on; `E21` supplies the ladder and heatmap components and their book-engine contract.

## Branch
`feat/replay-engine-book-replay`.

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` — SCR-097 Replay page, SCR-098 Replay session setup modal, SCR-099 Replay paper-trading results, SCR-044 "Go to date" dialog

title: Synchronise every pane to one replay clock, with a per-pane live opt-out
body:
## Context
Implements **US-RPL-005** (multi-pane synchronised replay, Should). Multi-timeframe study is only coherent if every pane shows the same moment, each at its own resolution — the story's NFR states it plainly: "replay clock is a single shared source of truth for all panes". The `23-ws-protocol.md` §11 note that live and replay subscriptions may coexist on one connection is what makes the opt-out ("keep live panes" on SCR-097) implementable without a second connection or a second code path.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Bind every pane in the replay workspace to the single session clock, so panes on different intervals all render the same replay timestamp at their own resolution.
- **Mixed symbols**: panes showing different symbols replay the same wall-clock moment; a symbol lacking recorded data at that moment shows an explicit state naming what is missing rather than an empty pane.
- **Per-pane live opt-out** (the SCR-097 "keep live panes" option): a pane can be marked live during replay, keeping a live subscription with a clear "live" badge while the others replay — implemented by subscribing that pane's topics without `replay_session_id`, disambiguated by `sub_id`.
- Visual disambiguation: replaying panes carry the REPLAY badge, live panes carry the live badge, and the two treatments must be distinguishable at a glance and without colour alone — this is the highest-risk confusion surface in the product, since both appear on one screen.
- Crosshair and range synchronisation across replaying panes reusing the existing E15/E11 pane-linking machinery (CMP-196 MultiChartLinker), with the replay timestamp as the sync source.
- Adding a pane mid-session subscribes it at the current cursor rather than at the window start.

## Out of scope
- Layout and workspace management (E15) — reused.
- The backend clock (E26-T03).
- Session persistence of the pane configuration (E26-S08).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Different intervals, one moment
  Given three panes on 1-minute, 5-minute and 15-minute intervals
  When replay is paused at a timestamp
  Then all three show that timestamp, each at its own resolution

Scenario: Mixed symbols share wall-clock time
  Given panes showing BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT
  Then both replay the same wall-clock moment
  And a symbol lacking data for that moment shows an explicit state naming what is missing

Scenario: A live pane beside replaying panes is unmistakable
  Given one pane is marked live during replay
  Then it keeps showing real-time data with a clear live badge
  And the replaying panes keep the REPLAY badge
  And the two are distinguishable without relying on colour

Scenario: A pane added mid-session joins at the cursor
  When a pane is added while replay is paused at 14:12
  Then it renders state as of 14:12, not from the window start

Scenario: Seeking moves every replaying pane and no live pane
  When the user seeks
  Then every replaying pane resynchronises to the new timestamp
  And any live pane is unaffected
```

## Technical notes / design
The clock is a single client-side store fed by the session state; panes subscribe to it rather than each tracking its own timestamp, which is what prevents the classic drift bug where one pane lags a seek.

A live pane during replay is a genuinely separate subscription on the same socket with the same topic name — `book.BTCUSDT.200` live and `book.BTCUSDT.200` replay are disambiguated by `sub_id` and the replay frames carry `rs` (`23-ws-protocol.md` §11). Panes must key their data stores by `sub_id`, not by topic name, or the two streams will merge into one corrupted view.

## Test plan
Unit: clock store fan-out, per-pane subscription mode selection, `sub_id` keying. Integration: three panes at different intervals seeking together; a mixed-symbol session where one symbol lacks coverage; a live pane alongside replaying panes asserting no cross-contamination of stores. E2E in E26-Q02. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
A live pane during replay means live market data and replayed data coexist on one screen: the badge treatment is a safety control, not decoration, and is verified in E26-D08 and E26-X03. Private topics remain non-replayable, so a live pane showing positions is unaffected by the replay session.

## Accessibility notes
Each pane's mode (REPLAY or live) is exposed as text in the pane's accessible name so a screen-reader user knows what they are reading without inspecting chrome; the missing-data state names the symbol and the moment.

## Performance notes
Budget #2's worst case is explicitly "all overlays + 5-symbol multi-chart layout + replay at 20x" — this story is the one that constructs that scenario, so its benchmark run feeds directly into the E26-Q03 measurement.

## Observability
Record pane count and mixed live/replay usage with replay analytics so the perf worst case is validated against real usage rather than assumed.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios automated or covered by a recorded manual step with follow-up.
- [ ] Store-keying regression test proving live and replay subscriptions to the same topic never merge.

title: Replay navigation aids, bookmarks and loop ranges
body:
## Context
Implements **US-RPL-007** (navigation aids, Should) and **US-RPL-008** (bookmarks and loops, Could). Without these, replay is a long tape with no index: the trader knows something interesting happened that morning but must scrub blindly to find it. US-RPL-007's NFR is the load-bearing constraint — "**event indexes are built at record time, not scanned at seek time**" — so jumping to the next stop-run must consult an index the recorder/detector pipeline already produced, never trigger a scan of the window.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Jump controls**: jump to the earliest available data, jump to a random recorded day, and jump to an absolute timestamp reusing **SCR-044 "Go to date"** (per its traceability entry, SCR-044 serves US-CHART-010 and US-RPL-007).
- **Event jump**: "next / previous big trade", "next / previous stop-run", and the other detector events exposed by E25, driven from the record-time event index; each jump issues a `seek` to the matching timestamp.
- The **no-matches state**: an explicit "no further matching events in the loaded range" message rather than a silent no-op.
- **Bookmarks** (US-RPL-008): set a bookmark at the current timestamp with a note (`B` hotkey), list them for quick navigation, navigate with `[` and `]`, rename and delete. Persisted per session in `replay_sessions.bookmarks` (jsonb) and user-scoped; render markers on the CMP-170 scrub track.
- **Bookmark on pruned data**: a bookmark whose referenced data has been pruned shows as unavailable with the reason and offers to remove itself.
- **Loop ranges**: set a loop start and end; playback repeats that range until stopped, driven by `replay_sessions.loop_enabled` and the clock's loop support from E26-T03; the loop range is visible on the scrub track.
- Bookmark export with the workspace (US-RPL-008 NFR) via the existing workspace export path.

## Out of scope
- Detector implementations and the event index itself (E25) — consumed. If the index is missing a needed event type, that is a ticket on E25.
- The chart's own "go to date" dialog (SCR-044 exists; this story reuses it).
- Backend loop mechanics (E26-T03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Jump to the earliest available data
  When the user chooses jump-to-earliest
  Then playback seeks to the earliest recorded timestamp in the session window
  And the resulting position is stated in text

Scenario: Event jump uses the index, not a scan
  Given a window containing three stop-run detections
  When the user chooses next stop-run twice
  Then playback seeks to the second and then the third detection
  And no full-window scan is performed, verified by the absence of a scan request and by the seek completing within the seek budget

Scenario: No further matches is explicit
  Given the cursor is past the last big trade in the range
  When the user chooses next big trade
  Then an explicit no-further-matching-events message is shown and the cursor does not move

Scenario: Bookmarks persist and navigate
  Given the user bookmarks 14:12 with a note
  Then it is saved for that session and symbol, listed for navigation, shown on the scrub track
  And the bracket keys navigate between bookmarks

Scenario: A bookmark on pruned data explains itself
  Given the data referenced by a bookmark has been pruned
  Then the bookmark shows as unavailable with the reason
  And it offers to remove itself

Scenario: A loop repeats until stopped
  Given a loop range 14:00-14:05 is set and playback is running
  Then playback repeats that range
  And the loop range is visible on the scrub track until the user clears it
```

## Technical notes / design
Bookmarks live in the session's `bookmarks jsonb` column (`ReplayBookmark` per `24-internal-schemas.md` §13.7) and are written via the session update path; they are user-scoped by the session's `user_id`. Because they are stored with the session, the resume flow in E26-S08 restores them for free.

Pruned-data detection for a bookmark compares its timestamp against current coverage at load time, not at click time, so the list is honest before the user acts.

Event jumps must be expressed as ordinary `seek` control calls so they inherit the seek budget, the seeking state and the coalescing behaviour rather than introducing a second navigation path.

## Test plan
Unit: jump target resolution, next/previous semantics at range boundaries, no-match state, bookmark CRUD and ordering, pruned-bookmark detection, loop wrap behaviour at the client. Integration: event jump against a fixture with known detector firings, asserting the index is consulted and the seek budget is met. E2E in E26-Q02. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
Bookmarks are user-scoped through the session (`replay:read`/`replay:write`, scope self) and their notes are free text rendered as text, never as markup — a stored-XSS surface if handled carelessly. Note length is bounded.

## Accessibility notes
Bookmark markers on the scrub track have text equivalents in the bookmark list; jump controls are labelled buttons with shortcut hints (`B`, `[`, `]`); the no-matches message is announced politely; the loop range is stated in text as well as drawn.

## Performance notes
Event jumps inherit the <=1 s p95 seek budget. The index lookup must be O(log n) or better over the window's event index; a linear scan at seek time violates the story's NFR and fails review.

## Observability
Analytics on jump-type usage and bookmark creation, so the detector event types traders actually navigate by are known and can be prioritised in E25's index.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios automated or covered by a recorded manual step with follow-up.
- [ ] Index-not-scan behaviour proven by a test asserting no scan request and a within-budget seek.
- [ ] Coverage >=80%; axe-core green; bookmark notes sanitised and length-bounded.
- [ ] QA sign-off; demoed; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E26-S02` supplies the transport and scrub track; `E25` supplies the detectors and the record-time event index that event jumps consult.

## Branch
`feat/replay-engine-navigation`.

title: Simulated trading in replay with hard isolation and the SCR-099 results drawer
body:
## Context
Implements **US-RPL-006** (simulated trading during replay, **Must**). This is the story that turns replay from observation into rehearsal — and it is the story where a mistake is worst, because it places an order ticket in front of a trader looking at market data from hours ago. The story's own scenario states the invariant: "**replay trades can never reach any exchange and are stored in a separate replay journal**".

Two mechanisms enforce it. Structurally, `24-internal-schemas.md` §13.7 determinism guarantee (4): `source="replay"` is set on every event so the OMS can refuse to route replay events to a live account *by construction*. Commercially and ethically, SCR-099's framing requirement: every figure is labelled simulated, the fill-model assumptions are stated, and the results are explicitly not a backtest guarantee (risk R12).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Attach the **PaperBridge**: when the session has `paper_account_id` set, route orders placed during replay to the local `PaperMatcher` (`24-internal-schemas.md` §12) with `ExecutionMode="replay"`, filling against the replayed book and prints and honouring the configured latency model (default 80 ms).
- Expose the order ticket inside the replay surface with distinctly simulated chrome per the E26-D02/E26-D04 specs; the ticket is the same component as live, not a fork, with its mode switched.
- **Isolation, enforced and tested**: no replay-originated order may reach any exchange adapter in any environment; replay fills are persisted with `is_paper=true` and an origin of `replay_sim` (`21-database-schema.md` `tg_origin` includes `replay_sim`), and are kept in a separate replay journal so they never mix with live or paper analytics (the story's NFR).
- **SCR-099 Replay paper-trading results drawer** per E26-D04: simulated fill list (CMP-049), P&L (CMP-116), equity curve (CMP-167), summary stats (CMP-168), export bar (CMP-099); the assumptions block stating the actual configured latency, slippage model, queue-position assumption and book source; the simulated badge in the heading; the non-dismissible not-a-backtest-guarantee caveat.
- **Promote to journal**: save the session as journal entries flagged `simulated=true`, excluded from live analytics by default, audited as `journal.simulated_import`.
- **Speed gating**: speeds above 25x disable paper fills with the reason stated (SCR-097 validation rule), because a modelled fill at 100x is not meaningful.
- The insufficient-liquidity case surfaced honestly when the replayed book is exhausted (`INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY` from the matcher).

## Out of scope
- The paper matcher's fill model, queue modelling and demo/live parity (E38) — consumed; the assumptions block *reports* its configuration.
- Journal and analytics screens (E41) — linked into.
- Rule simulation over replay (E35).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: An order during replay is filled by the simulator
  Given a replay session with a paper account attached
  When the user places an order during replay
  Then it is filled by the simulator using the replayed book and prints
  And the configured latency model is applied to the fill

Scenario: Nothing reaches an exchange, ever
  Given any order placed during replay, in any environment
  When the order path is exercised including adversarial attempts to re-tag the order as live
  Then no exchange adapter call is made
  And the attempt is rejected structurally on the source="replay" marker, not by a UI check

Scenario: Replay results never mix with real analytics
  Given simulated fills from a replay session
  When live or paper analytics are queried
  Then replay fills are excluded by default
  And they are retrievable only from the replay journal or as explicitly flagged simulated journal entries

Scenario: The results drawer is honest
  When a replay session ends with simulated fills
  Then the results drawer shows the simulated badge in the heading, the actual configured latency and fill model, and the non-dismissible not-a-backtest-guarantee caveat
  And every figure sits under a heading carrying the simulated framing

Scenario: Paper fills are disabled above the supported speed
  Given the user sets speed above 25x with paper fills enabled
  Then paper fills are disabled with the reason stated

Scenario: An exhausted book is reported, not faked
  Given a market order larger than the replayed book depth
  Then the fill is rejected with an insufficient-liquidity reason shown to the user
```

## Technical notes / design
`ExecutionMode` and `Environment` are orthogonal (`24-internal-schemas.md` §2): a paper fill during a replay of live-recorded data is `environment="live", execution_mode="replay"`, persisted as `is_paper=true`. The UI must not collapse these into a single "replay environment" label, and the journal must not attribute a replay fill to the live environment's P&L.

The isolation check belongs at the OMS boundary, not in the UI: the UI's simulated chrome is a usability measure, while the structural refusal on `source="replay"` is the control. E26-X02 probes it adversarially.

Ship behind a feature flag defaulting off until E38's matcher is available, so the rest of the epic is not blocked by it.

## Test plan
Unit: bridge wiring, speed gating, assumptions-block rendering from actual configuration, results aggregation. Integration: place, fill, cancel and reject flows against the replayed book, asserting zero adapter calls via a spy on every adapter method; journal separation queries. Security: the adversarial re-tagging attempt from E26-X02 is run as a required test here too. E2E in E26-Q02. Coverage >=80% frontend and >=85% on any touched backend bridge code.

## Security notes
This is the epic's highest-severity control. Threats: a replay order routed to a real account (financial loss), replay fills polluting live analytics (bad decisions downstream), and a simulated result exported without its flag (misrepresentation). Controls: structural `source="replay"` refusal at the OMS, `is_paper=true` plus `origin='replay_sim'` persistence, separate replay journal, `simulated=true` on every export, and audit of `journal.simulated_import`. Replay paper fills are tagged `simulated=true` and **never enter the trading audit stream** (SCR-097/098 analytics notes). Requires Security engineer review before Done (E26-X03).

## Accessibility notes
Per SCR-099: results are a table plus a summary description list; every chart has a table alternative; the simulated badge is in the heading so screen-reader users meet it before any number; the ticket's simulated mode is announced in its accessible name, not only by colour.

## Performance notes
Results are computed server-side at session end and fetched once; no live subscriptions remain open when the drawer is shown. The drawer virtualises beyond 500 fills.

## Observability
`replay.paper_fill` (tagged `simulated=true`, never in the real order audit), `replay.results_viewed`, `replay.results_exported`, `replay.results_promoted_to_journal`; a counter of blocked live-routing attempts, which should always be zero in production and is alerted on if it is not.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios automated, including the adversarial no-exchange-call assertion.
- [ ] Journal separation verified by query-level tests.
- [ ] SCR-099 sign-off checklist satisfied; assumptions copy factually reviewed by the E38 lead.
- [ ] Coverage thresholds met; axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass on SCR-099.
- [ ] security: Security engineer review comment present (E26-X03); abuse-case check performed.
- [ ] QA sign-off; demoed; feature-flag state recorded (default off until E38 lands).
- [ ] PRs merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E26-S04` supplies the replayed book the matcher fills against; `E38` supplies the `PaperMatcher`; `E26-X02` supplies the isolation abuse cases this story must pass.

## Branch

title: Restore replay position, speed and pane configuration across machines
body:
## Context
Implements **US-RPL-009** (replay session state restore, Should). A study session is long: the trader steps through an hour of tape, gets interrupted, and must be able to come back. The story's NFR makes it explicitly server-side — "state stored server-side per user so it follows them across machines" — which the `replay_sessions` table already supports via `cursor_ts`, `speed`, `state` and `bookmarks`.

The honest-failure requirement matters as much as the happy path: recorded data has a 30-day default retention, so a resumed session frequently points at data that no longer exists.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Persist replay session state server-side: `cursor_ts` (throttled to at most 1 write/s by E26-T01), `speed`, `state`, `bookmarks`, `loop_enabled`, plus the pane configuration needed to restore the workspace (stored with the workspace/layout per E15, referenced from the session).
- On reopening replay for a symbol, offer resume with the stored symbol, timestamp, speed and pane configuration, restoring all four.
- **Data-changed path**: when the underlying data was pruned since, tell the user what changed and offer the nearest available start point rather than failing or silently moving the cursor.
- **Start fresh**: clear the saved replay state for that symbol explicitly.
- Handle the reclaimed-session case (2 h idle -> `finished`): resuming recreates a session at the stored cursor rather than surfacing a dead id.
- Surface restore from the SCR-098 setup modal (the resume affordance built in E26-S01) and from the `/replay` route's entry state.

## Out of scope
- The session store and idle reclaim mechanics (E26-T01).
- Workspace/layout persistence itself (E15) — referenced.
- Bookmarks CRUD (E26-S06) — restored, not defined here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Resume restores everything that matters
  Given the user closed the app mid-replay at 14:12 at speed 4x with three panes
  When they reopen the replay
  Then the symbol, timestamp, speed and pane configuration are restored

Scenario: Resuming across machines works
  Given a session position saved on one machine
  When the same user opens replay on another machine
  Then the same position, speed and bookmarks are offered

Scenario: Pruned data is explained and an alternative offered
  Given the underlying data was pruned since the session was saved
  When the user attempts to resume
  Then they are told what changed
  And the nearest available start point is offered

Scenario: Start fresh really clears state
  When the user chooses start fresh
  Then the saved replay state for that symbol is cleared
  And reopening offers no stale resume

Scenario: A reclaimed session resumes without a dead id
  Given the server reclaimed the session after idle timeout
  When the user resumes
  Then a new session is created at the stored cursor position transparently
```

## Technical notes / design
The cursor written during playback is throttled server-side; on a clean pause or page unload, flush the exact cursor so resume is precise rather than up to a second stale. On an unclean exit the stored cursor may lag by up to a second, which is acceptable and must not be presented as exact.

Pruned-data detection compares the stored `range_start`/`cursor_ts` against current coverage from `GET /market/data-coverage` at resume time, reusing the same logic as the SCR-098 range validation rather than duplicating it.

## Test plan
Unit: restore payload assembly, pruned-data comparison, start-fresh clearing, reclaimed-session recreation. Integration: save, reclaim, resume against a stubbed API; cross-user isolation (user B cannot resume user A's session). E2E in E26-Q02. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
Session state is scoped to the owning user (`replay:read`/`replay:write`, scope self); a resume request for another user's session returns not-found rather than forbidden. No filesystem paths are stored or restored (SR-097). Restored pane configuration must be validated on load rather than trusted, since it is user-controlled persisted data.

## Accessibility notes
The resume offer is a labelled choice with the stored position stated in text (absolute time, not "where you left off"); the data-changed explanation names the affected range; Start fresh is clearly distinguished from Resume in both label and focus order.

## Performance notes
Cursor persistence is bounded to <=1 write/s per session so 100x playback does not generate a write storm; resume must complete within the same seek budget as a manual seek to the same point.

## Observability
Analytics on resume versus start-fresh choice and on the pruned-data path frequency — the latter is a direct signal about whether the default 30-day retention matches how people actually study.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios automated or covered by a recorded manual step with follow-up.
- [ ] Cross-user isolation test green.
- [ ] Coverage >=80%; axe-core green; resume choice screen-reader verified.
- [ ] QA sign-off; demoed; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E26-S05` supplies the pane configuration that restore must reinstate; `E26-S06` supplies the bookmarks restored alongside the position.

## Branch
`feat/replay-engine-session-restore`.
