title: Write the black-box test plan for replay sessions, playback and fidelity
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 requires a QA-executed black-box test plan with a per-scenario pass/fail sign-off before any Story reaches Done, and §8 makes that non-skippable. E26 needs its plan written early because several of its most important behaviours are *absences* — no dropped events, no silent gap, no exchange call, no replay data in live analytics — and absences are only tested if someone deliberately writes them down.

`30-release-roadmap.md` §6.4 also assigns E26 a named honesty checklist item: every recorder-dependent view must show an explicit partial-history state naming the first available timestamp.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A black-box test plan at `docs/qa/plans/e26-replay.md` covering, per story group:
  1. **Session lifecycle** (US-RPL-001, US-RPL-009): create over covered / uncovered / partially covered windows; start before available history; preparation progress and cancel; resume; resume after prune; start fresh; idle reclaim and resume of a reclaimed session; quota exhaustion.
  2. **Playback and transport** (US-RPL-004): every speed preset and a custom value; play/pause; step bar; step tick; jump one minute; jump to real time with confirmation; scrub-drag seek; end of range; every hotkey in the SCR-097 table.
  3. **Fidelity and honesty** (US-RPL-002, US-RPL-003): tick stepping updating every dependent view; no-tick-data fallback; achieved-rate reporting at 100x; book/heatmap reconstruction; not-recorded state for book streams; depth honesty; recorder gap encountered with Skip gap and Stop here.
  4. **Multi-pane** (US-RPL-005): different intervals; mixed symbols; a live pane beside replaying panes; pane added mid-session.
  5. **Navigation** (US-RPL-007, US-RPL-008): jump to earliest, random day, go-to-date; event jumps; no-match message; bookmark create/navigate/rename/delete/pruned; loop range.
  6. **Paper trading in replay** (US-RPL-006): fills against the replayed book; speed gating above 25x; insufficient liquidity; results drawer framing; promote to journal; isolation from live analytics.
- An **exploratory charter set**: "try to confuse replay with live"; "try to make the scrubber lie about coverage"; "try to make a pane disagree with the clock"; "try to get a simulated figure to appear without its framing"; each timeboxed with a debrief note.
- Entry/exit criteria, environment and fixture requirements (naming the E26-T06 golden fixtures), and the defect-triage convention for this epic (a missing honesty state is a **P1**, matching the R2 rule that a missing "(estimated)" badge is P1, not cosmetic).
- The sign-off template QA will use per story.

## Out of scope
- Test automation (E26-Q02), perf scripts (E26-Q03), chaos (E26-Q04), a11y audit (E26-Q05).
- Determinism verification (E26-T06) — the plan references it rather than duplicating it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every RPL story has coverage
  Given US-RPL-001 to US-RPL-009
  When the plan is reviewed
  Then each story's Gherkin scenarios map to at least one plan case
  And each case names its expected observable result

Scenario: Absences are explicitly tested
  Given the behaviours defined as absences
  Then the plan contains explicit cases for no dropped events, no silent gap, no exchange call and no replay data in live analytics

Scenario: Fixtures are named, not assumed
  Then every case names the fixture or environment state it requires, referencing the E26-T06 golden fixtures
```

## Technical notes / design
The plan must distinguish cases executable against the synthetic feed (`CV_FEED=synthetic`, which replays `packages/fixtures/raw`) from those requiring a real recorded fixture, since E2E always runs against synthetic or demo and never live (`20-architecture.md` §dev environment).

## Test plan
The deliverable is itself the test plan; it is reviewed by the E26 tech lead and the CDO track for design-state coverage before being used as a gate.

## Security notes
The plan includes the abuse cases from E26-X02 by reference so a QA pass exercises them too, rather than leaving them solely to the security track.

## Accessibility notes
The plan references the E26-Q05 a11y audit rather than duplicating it, but each UI case notes whether it must be executed keyboard-only.

## Performance notes
Perf cases are referenced from E26-Q03; the black-box plan records the user-observable expectations (seek feels bounded, no frozen UI, achieved rate shown) rather than the numeric budgets.

## Observability
Each case notes the analytics/audit event it should produce, so instrumentation gaps are found by QA rather than after release.

- [ ] Plan merged at `docs/qa/plans/e26-replay.md` and linked from every E26 story.

- [ ] Exploratory charters written with timeboxes.

title: Automate the Playwright E2E suite for replay setup, playback and navigation
body:
## Context
The replay surfaces are stateful in a way unit tests cannot cover: a session is created, buffered, played, seeked, interrupted by a gap and ended, with every pane expected to agree at each step. `03-testing-strategy.md` places E2E (Playwright, web and Electron) at the top of the pyramid for exactly these journeys, and `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` requires the suite to be a gating check.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright specs covering the journeys from the E26-Q01 plan, run in both the web and Electron shells:
  1. Create a session from SCR-098 over a covered window and reach playing state.
  2. Uncovered window refused with the documented message; start-before-history offered and accepted.
  3. Play, pause, step bar, step tick, change speed, jump one minute, and every SCR-097 hotkey.
  4. Scrub-drag seek with all panes resynchronising to the same timestamp.
  5. Gap encountered with Skip gap and with Stop here.
  6. End of range and the WS `revoked` handling.
  7. Multi-pane: three intervals synchronised; one pane kept live with both badges asserted.
  8. Navigation: jump to earliest, event jump, no-match message, bookmark create/navigate, loop set and observed.
  9. Paper trading: place an order in replay, assert a simulated fill, assert zero exchange calls via a network assertion, reach SCR-099 and assert the simulated framing and caveat are present.
  10. Resume: reload mid-session and restore position, speed and panes; resume after prune.
- Deterministic fixtures: drive from the synthetic feed (`CV_FEED=synthetic`) and the E26-T06 golden fixtures so runs are reproducible; no test may depend on wall-clock timing beyond explicit waits on observable state.
- A **replay-vs-live confusion assertion**: a visual-regression check on the REPLAY chrome so a future change that weakens it fails CI rather than a review.
- Wire into the CI E2E job with appropriate tagging so the slower replay journeys can run on the nightly tier while the core ones gate PRs.

## Out of scope
- Perf and soak (E26-Q03), chaos (E26-Q04), a11y audit (E26-Q05).
- Backend determinism (E26-T06).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The suite is deterministic
  Given the suite is run ten times against the synthetic feed
  Then it passes ten times with no flaky retries recorded

Scenario: The isolation invariant is asserted at the E2E layer
  Given the paper-trading journey
  When an order is placed during replay
  Then a network assertion proves no exchange-bound request was made

Scenario: Chrome weakening is caught automatically
  Given the visual-regression baseline for the REPLAY chrome
  When the chrome treatment changes
  Then the check fails and requires an explicit baseline update with review

Scenario: Both shells are covered
  Then the core journeys run in web and in Electron
```

## Technical notes / design
Wait on observable application state (session state text, pane timestamps) rather than on fixed timeouts; replay's variable speeds make timeout-based waits inherently flaky. For the seek journeys, assert on the settled timestamp shared by all panes rather than on intermediate frames.

## Test plan
The suite is the deliverable; its own quality bar is the ten-run stability criterion plus a documented triage path for any flake, which must be fixed rather than retried.

## Security notes
The zero-exchange-call assertion is a security control expressed as a test and must not be weakened to a warning. Test fixtures contain no real credentials; E2E never runs against live (`20-architecture.md` §dev environment).

## Accessibility notes
The suite includes an axe-core scan on SCR-097, SCR-098 and SCR-099 as a smoke gate; the full audit remains E26-Q05.

## Performance notes
Keep the PR-tier suite within the agreed CI budget by tagging the long journeys (100x soak-adjacent, full-day windows) to the nightly tier.

## Observability
Publish traces and videos for failed runs as CI artefacts; record suite runtime so growth is visible.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All listed journeys implemented and green in web and Electron.
- [ ] Ten-run stability demonstrated; no retry-masking configured.
- [ ] Visual-regression baseline for the REPLAY chrome committed with an update procedure requiring review.
- [ ] Wired into CI with PR and nightly tiers; documented in the testing docs.

title: Build replay performance, 100x soak and seek-budget benchmarks as CI gates
body:
## Context
Two budgets in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` name replay explicitly. Budget **#2** defines the worst case as "all overlays + 5-symbol multi-chart layout + **replay at 20x**" with a hard never-below-30fps rule. Budget **#15** requires sustaining **up to 100x** without violating the frame floor, crash-free and desync-free, with visual fidelity allowed to degrade but not silently. Roadmap exit criterion #8 adds the 1 s scrub target for a 200-depth symbol.

Budgets that are measured once and then forgotten do not hold. `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and the R5 hardening plan both require budgets promoted to CI-enforced checks with regression alarms; this ticket does that for replay.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Frame-budget benchmark** for the budget #2 worst case: 5-symbol multi-chart layout with footprint, profile, heatmap, bubbles, three stat rows and a CVD pane, replaying at 20x; report p95 frame time and the minimum fps over the run.
- **100x soak** (budget #15): replay a recorded 24 h symbol-day at 100x; assert crash-free, desync-free, zero dropped events, flat memory, and record the achieved rate profile over the run.
- **Seek benchmark**: 50 seeks to uniformly random targets on a 200-depth symbol-day; report p50/p95/max total and the stage breakdown from `replay_seek_duration_ms{stage}`; gate on p95 <1 s and max <2 s.
- **Source throughput benchmark** carried forward from E26-K01: sustained events/s per tier plus the straddling-window case, gated against the K01 baseline with an agreed regression threshold.
- **Tick-fidelity benchmark**: SCR-097's stated requirement of 25x on 1-minute data and 4x on raw tick data without dropped frames.
- Promote all of the above to CI: PR tier runs the short-form benchmarks, nightly runs the soak; regression alarms configured against recorded baselines with a documented procedure for accepting a new baseline (requires the Architect).
- A benchmark report committed per run under the perf results location used by the rest of the programme.

## Out of scope
- Fixing regressions found (Bugs against the owning epic).
- Backend ingestion soak (E16) and WS load profiles (E17) — replay benchmarks reuse their harnesses where applicable rather than rebuilding them.
- Chaos scenarios (E26-Q04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The worst case is measured, not assumed
  Given the budget #2 worst-case scene replaying at 20x
  When the benchmark runs
  Then p95 frame time and minimum fps are recorded
  And the run fails if fps drops below 30 at any point

Scenario: 100x is crash-free and lossless
  Given a recorded 24 h symbol-day replayed at 100x
  Then the run completes without crash or desync
  And zero events are dropped and memory is flat across the run

Scenario: Seek holds its budget
  Given 50 random-target seeks on a 200-depth symbol-day
  Then p95 is under 1 s and max is under 2 s
  And the per-stage breakdown is reported so a regression is attributable

Scenario: Regressions alarm rather than accumulate
  Given a committed baseline
  When a change regresses any gated metric beyond its threshold
  Then CI fails and a new baseline can only be accepted with Architect approval
```

## Technical notes / design
Run on the standard CI perf runner with the machine profile recorded in every report; comparisons are only valid within a profile. The frame benchmark uses the engine benchmark harness established in E11 rather than a replay-specific one, so replay is measured with the same instrument as everything else.

The 100x soak's "flat memory" assertion samples periodically rather than comparing endpoints, so a mid-run leak that is later collected is still visible.

## Test plan
This ticket is a test deliverable; its own validation is a deliberate regression injected behind a flag to prove each gate actually fails.

## Security notes
Resource-exhaustion limits from E26-T01 must remain enforced during the benchmarks; a benchmark that disables them would measure a configuration that cannot exist in production. Record the limits in effect in each report.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
This ticket *is* the performance deliverable for E26 and produces the evidence cited in the epic DoD and in the R2 PRR.

## Observability
Benchmarks consume the E26-T07 metric set, which also validates that the metrics are correct and complete; discrepancies found here are fixed in T07.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All five benchmarks implemented, with baselines committed and machine profiles recorded.
- [ ] Gates wired into CI at the PR and nightly tiers with regression alarms.
- [ ] Deliberate-regression validation proves each gate fails when it should.
- [ ] Budget #2, budget #15 and the seek target results recorded in the E26 perf report.
- [ ] Baseline-acceptance procedure documented and agreed with the Architect.

title: Chaos scenarios for replay: gaps, pruning, slow consumers, restarts, expiry
body:
## Context
`03-testing-strategy.md` and the R2 quality gates require chaos/failover coverage, and replay's failure modes are distinctive: its data source can disappear underneath it (retention pruning), its consumers can stall (a slow client at 100x), its sessions can be reclaimed mid-study, and its windows routinely contain recorder gaps. `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.4 lists the required integration fixtures: normal session, high-volatility burst, WS disconnect plus resync, sequence gap, thin-book symbol.

The defining property under test is the one from `24-internal-schemas.md` §13.7: under backpressure the clock slows — **replay must never lose data**.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Chaos scenarios, automated and runnable on demand:
  1. **Recorder gap mid-window**: assert the gap is reported at the boundary with both Skip gap and Stop here honoured, `gap_warnings` incremented, and derived views showing the partial-history state rather than interpolating.
  2. **Retention prune during an active session**: data underlying the remainder of the window is pruned mid-playback; assert a clear failure state naming what is gone, no crash, and no fabricated data.
  3. **Slow consumer at high speed**: a client accepting at a fraction of the required rate; assert the clock slows, the achieved rate is reported, and **zero events are dropped**.
  4. **Client WS disconnect and reconnect mid-replay**: assert resubscription restores the session at the correct cursor with fresh snapshots, and that no duplicate events are applied.
  5. **Backend restart mid-session**: assert the session is either recoverable at its persisted cursor or fails cleanly with a resume offer — never a silently wrong position.
  6. **Idle reclaim during a study pause**: assert the session-expired state and a working resume.
  7. **Storage tier unavailable** (QuestDB or the Parquet path fails mid-read): assert a clear error state and clean buffer release rather than a hang.
  8. **Thin-book symbol and high-volatility burst** fixtures replayed end to end to assert no assumption of dense data.
- Each scenario records observed behaviour against expected, and feeds any divergence back as a Bug with priority.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the defects found.
- Upstream exchange chaos (E17/E08) — replay reads recorded data and does not talk to Bybit.
- Perf benchmarking (E26-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Backpressure never loses data
  Given a consumer accepting at one quarter of the required rate at 20x
  When the scenario runs to completion
  Then every recorded event is delivered in order
  And the achieved rate is reported lower than requested

Scenario: Pruning mid-session fails honestly
  Given retention prunes the remainder of the window during playback
  Then the session reports what is no longer available
  And no fabricated or interpolated data is rendered

Scenario: Reconnect resumes without duplication
  Given a client WS disconnect at 14:12 during playback
  When the client reconnects and resubscribes
  Then it resumes from the correct cursor with fresh snapshots
  And no event is applied twice

Scenario: A failing storage tier releases cleanly
  Given the cold tier becomes unavailable mid-read
  Then the session enters an error state with a clear message and its buffers are released
  And no request hangs indefinitely
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the §6.4 fixture set. Fault injection is applied at the repository and transport boundaries rather than by killing processes where possible, so the scenarios are reproducible in CI; the backend-restart scenario is the exception and runs in the nightly integration environment.

## Test plan
Each scenario is an automated integration test with a recorded expected-behaviour narrative; the nightly tier runs all eight, and the PR tier runs the three cheapest (gap, slow consumer, reconnect).

## Security notes
The slow-consumer and storage-failure scenarios double as availability tests for the resource-exhaustion threat: assert that a stalled or failing session releases its memory and task budget rather than pinning them, which is the mechanism a malicious or careless client would otherwise exploit.

## Accessibility notes
Each failure state surfaced by these scenarios must be verified as text reachable by assistive technology, not only as a visual treatment — checked jointly with E26-Q05.

## Performance notes
The slow-consumer scenario also produces the achieved-rate curve referenced by the E26-Q03 soak.

## Observability
Every scenario asserts the expected metric movement (`replay_gap_warnings_total`, `replay_backpressure_seconds_total`, `replay_clock_lag_ms`), so observability gaps are found here rather than during an incident.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All eight scenarios automated with expected-behaviour narratives recorded.
- [ ] Zero-event-loss under backpressure proven.
- [ ] Divergences filed as Bugs with priority and linked.
- [ ] Wired into the nightly integration job with the three cheapest also on PRs.

## Dependencies
`E26-T03` owns the backpressure and gap behaviour under test; `E26-Q01` frames the expectations.

title: Accessibility audit of SCR-097, SCR-098, SCR-099 and the replay components
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 makes WCAG 2.2 AA default-on for every UI surface with no "internal tool" exception, and `05-accessibility-standard.md` requires axe-core in CI plus manual screen-reader passes. Replay is unusually demanding: a continuously updating clock, a slider whose value is a timestamp, an animated playhead, and a mode indicator whose failure has a trading consequence.

The R2 a11y gate also requires that the DOM ladder and footprint remain reachable and announced under replay exactly as under live — replay must not quietly break the accessibility of the panels it hosts.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Automated **axe-core** scans of SCR-097, SCR-098 and SCR-099 in every state reachable without fault injection, in light, dark and high-contrast themes, at every supported density, wired as a CI gate.
- **Manual screen-reader passes** with NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on macOS covering: creating a session, starting playback, hearing the clock (verifying the 1 Hz cap and polite politeness), operating the scrub slider and hearing `aria-valuetext` as absolute time, stepping by bar and tick, encountering a gap and choosing an action, reaching end of range, and reading the SCR-099 results including the simulated framing in the heading.
- **Keyboard-only pass** over the complete SCR-097 hotkey table plus tab order through the transport, the scrub control and back to the panel region, verifying no focus trap and visible focus throughout, and resolving the slider-arrow versus global-arrow collision documented in E26-D06.
- **Reduced-motion verification**: with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, confirm each animation's specified fallback and that no information is lost.
- **Contrast measurement** of the REPLAY chrome, the live badge, coverage shading and the simulated badge in all themes (4.5:1 text, 3:1 non-text).
- **Non-colour-carrier verification** for: REPLAY versus live, coverage recorded/partial/missing, and simulated versus real figures.
- **Panel a11y under replay**: confirm the E18 footprint DOM mirror and the E21 ladder remain reachable and correctly announced while replaying.
- Findings filed as Bugs with severity, re-verified after fixes; an audit report recorded on the ticket.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the defects (filed to the owning stories).
- Design-phase a11y review (E26-D06) — this audits the built result against it.
- Panel-internal a11y ownership (E18/E21) beyond confirming replay does not regress it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Automated scans are clean and gating
  Given axe-core scans of SCR-097, SCR-098 and SCR-099 in all themes and densities
  Then there are zero serious or critical violations
  And the scan is a CI gate rather than a report

Scenario: The clock does not flood the screen reader
  Given playback at 20x with a screen reader active
  Then the clock is announced at most once per second and politely
  And the visual readout may update more often without affecting announcements

Scenario: The slider speaks in time, not numbers
  When the scrub slider receives focus and is moved
  Then aria-valuetext announces an absolute human-readable timestamp

Scenario: Mode is never colour-only
  Given a simulated colour-vision deficiency and a greyscale rendering
  Then REPLAY versus live, coverage states and simulated versus real figures all remain distinguishable

Scenario: Replay does not regress panel accessibility
  Given the footprint DOM mirror and the DOM ladder under replay
  Then both are reachable and announced exactly as under live
```

## Technical notes / design
Fault-injected states (gap, expiry, prune) are reached using the E26-Q04 harness so the audit covers them rather than skipping them as unreachable — these error states are precisely where accessibility is usually neglected.

## Test plan
Automated scans plus scripted manual passes with a recorded transcript per pass. Every finding gets a severity, an owner and a re-verification record.

## Security notes
Confirm that accessible names and live-region announcements do not leak account identifiers, session ids or internal paths — assistive-technology output is an often-forgotten disclosure channel.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility deliverable for the build phase of E26 and provides the evidence for the epic DoD's a11y line.

## Performance notes
Confirm the announcement throttling does not itself cost frame budget (announcement work must not run per frame).

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] axe-core gate green on all three screens in all themes and densities.
- [ ] NVDA and VoiceOver passes recorded with transcripts.
- [ ] Keyboard-only pass complete with the arrow-key collision resolved and documented.
- [ ] Reduced-motion and contrast verifications recorded.
- [ ] All findings filed with severity and re-verified after fixes.
- [ ] Accessibility specialist sign-off recorded.

## Dependencies
`E26-Q02` provides the E2E harness whose axe smoke gate this extends; `E26-S07` completes SCR-099, the last surface to audit.

title: Assemble the replay regression pack, run charters and record epic QA sign-off
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires an epic-level QA pass — "a regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded, not just child-ticket QA" — before an Epic can be Done, and the R2 PRR depends on it. This ticket is the gate that closes E26.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Regression pack**: distil the E26-Q01 plan and the automated suites into a repeatable pack that runs against any future release, tagged by story, covering the honesty behaviours (gap states, not-recorded states, partial history, achieved rate, simulated framing) and the isolation invariant. Add it to the programme-wide regression suite so replay is re-verified in R3, R4 and R5.
- **Execute the exploratory charters** from E26-Q01 with debrief notes: replay-versus-live confusion, scrubber coverage honesty, pane-versus-clock disagreement, unframed simulated figures. Timeboxed, with findings filed.
- **Cross-epic verification** that replay did not regress the surfaces it hosts: run the E18 footprint, E19 profile, E20 Deep-Stats, E21 DOM/heatmap, E23 CVD and E25 detector regression packs *under replay* and confirm parity with their live results, closing roadmap exit criterion #1 from the QA side as well as the CI side.
- **Epic QA sign-off record**: per-story pass/fail from the black-box plan, the state of every quality gate (determinism suite, perf gates, chaos results, a11y audit, security sign-off), open defects with severity and disposition, and an explicit statement of any QA-capacity deviations.
- Confirm the R2 §6.4 honesty checklist for every replay-hosted view.

## Out of scope
- Writing new automation (Q02/Q03/Q04).
- Fixing defects — filed and tracked, with P0/P1 blocking this sign-off.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  Given the E26-Q01 plan
  When the pack is executed
  Then every case has a recorded pass/fail with evidence
  And the epic sign-off states the aggregate result

  When they are run under replay
  Then their results match the live runs
  And any divergence is filed against the owning epic and blocks this sign-off if P0 or P1

Scenario: No P0 or P1 remains open
  When sign-off is attempted with an open P0 or P1 in E26 scope
  Then sign-off is refused until it is resolved or explicitly accepted by the Owner

Scenario: The regression pack outlives the epic

```

## Technical notes / design
Running the hosted epics' packs under replay is the cheapest possible check on the single-code-path claim from a black-box angle, and it catches the class of bug where a view quietly special-cases replay somewhere deep in a component.

## Test plan
Manual execution of the pack plus a supervised run of the automated suites; results recorded with evidence per case.

## Security notes
Includes a QA-side confirmation of the E26-X02 abuse cases (no exchange call from replay, no cross-user session access, no path input accepted), independent of the security track's own testing — two independent confirmations for the epic's highest-severity invariant.

## Accessibility notes
The a11y audit result from E26-Q05 is a required input; an unresolved serious or critical violation blocks sign-off.

## Performance notes
The E26-Q03 gate results are a required input; a failing perf gate blocks sign-off unless the Architect records an accepted deviation.

## Observability
Confirm every analytics and audit event listed across the epic actually fires, using the observability dashboards from E26-T07.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Regression pack assembled, registered in the programme suite and scheduled for future trains.
- [ ] Exploratory charters executed with debrief notes.
- [ ] Hosted-view packs run under replay with parity confirmed.
- [ ] Epic QA sign-off comment recorded with per-story results and gate status.
- [ ] Zero open P0/P1 in E26 scope, or explicit Owner acceptance recorded.

All E26 QA tickets, the final story `E26-S08`, the design QA sweep `E26-D08` and the security sign-off `E26-X03` must complete first.

title: STRIDE threat model and abuse cases for the replay engine and its data access
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §6.4 names E26 explicitly in the R2 security gate: "STRIDE for E26 (**replay resource exhaustion, path handling for archived data**) and E21". `04-security-program.md` already carries the relevant pre-assessed threat, **S3 — elevation of privilege: "Replay/export endpoint used to read arbitrary filesystem paths"**, rated High and mitigated by **SR-097**. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 requires the STRIDE kickoff before the epic can be Ready.

This ticket runs the model properly rather than inheriting the two headline threats, because replay has a third that is easy to miss: it is the only feature that presents a trading interface over stale data.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE model for the replay data flow — client -> REST control -> session store -> source readers (QuestDB, Parquet/DuckDB) -> clock -> injector -> bus -> WS gateway -> client, plus the paper-matcher branch — recorded at `docs/plan/27-adrs/` adjacent security notes or the security-program appendix as the programme convention dictates, and linked here.
- Threats enumerated per element, at minimum:
  - **Spoofing**: using another user's `replay_session_id` on a WS subscription.
  - **Tampering**: modifying a session's window or paper account to read or trade against data the user is not entitled to; tampering with stored bookmarks or pane configuration (user-controlled persisted data replayed into the client).
  - **Repudiation**: a simulated fill being indistinguishable from a real one in the journal or in an export.
  - **Information disclosure**: path traversal or symlink escape into the Parquet archive (**S3/SR-097**); error messages leaking internal paths or dataset ids; accessible names or live regions leaking identifiers.
  - **Denial of service**: unbounded window, many concurrent sessions, seek amplification via scrub-drag, read-ahead memory growth from a stalled consumer, 100x playback CPU cost — the "replay resource exhaustion" the roadmap names.
  - **Elevation of privilege**: a replay-sourced event routed to a live account; a private topic subscribed under a replay session; a paper account the caller has not been granted.
- **Abuse cases** written as executable test intentions for E26-X02, each with an expected refusal.
- Risk ratings with likelihood and impact, mapped to the existing controls (SR-097, RBAC scope self, the T01 quotas, the T03 `source="replay"` invariant) and any new control required.
- Data classification confirmation: recorded market data is A-10 with integrity objective O8; session metadata references accounts.

## Out of scope
- Implementing controls (T01/T02/T03/T05 own them; new gaps are filed as tickets).
- Penetration testing (programme-level, before Live enablement).
- The recorder's own threat model (E16-X01) — referenced, not repeated.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every element and every STRIDE category is considered
  Given the replay data-flow diagram
  When the model is reviewed by the Security engineer and the Architect
  Then each element has each STRIDE category either enumerated with a threat or explicitly marked not-applicable with a reason

Scenario: The roadmap's two named threats are addressed in depth
  Then replay resource exhaustion and path handling for archived data each have threats, ratings and named controls
  And each control maps to a specific implementation ticket

Scenario: Abuse cases are executable
  Then every abuse case states the attempt, the expected refusal and the layer that refuses it
  And E26-X02 can implement them without further interpretation

Scenario: Gaps become tickets
```

title: Implement replay abuse-case tests, path-safety controls and SAST/DAST rules
body:
## Context
The controls E26-X01 identifies are only real if they are tested adversarially and continuously. SR-097 states the requirement in the imperative: replay and export endpoints "MUST NOT accept filesystem paths; datasets are addressed by registry ids. **Path traversal and symlink escape tests are mandatory.**" The isolation invariant — no replay event reaching an exchange — deserves the same treatment, since it is the only thing standing between a rehearsal and a real order.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Abuse-case test suite** implementing every case from E26-X01, at minimum:
  1. Subscribe with another user's `replay_session_id` -> rejected with `replay_session_not_found`, with no confirmation that the session exists.
  2. REST fetch, control and delete of another user's session -> not-found, not forbidden.
  3. Create a session naming a `paper_account_id` the caller has not been granted -> rejected.
  4. Subscribe `orders` / `positions` / `executions` / `wallet` with `replay_session_id` -> `invalid_options`.
  5. Place an order during replay and attempt to re-tag it as live at every layer -> refused structurally on the `source="replay"` marker; assert zero exchange-adapter calls via method-level spies.
  6. Request a window exceeding the window cap, or exceed the concurrent-session quota -> rejected before buffer allocation.
  7. Scrub-drag seek storm -> coalesced and rate-limited; assert bounded work and no unbounded task growth.
  8. Stalled consumer -> read-ahead bounded, memory flat, session reclaimable.
  9. Oversized or malformed bookmark notes and pane configuration -> bounded, sanitised, and safe when restored into the client.
- **Path-safety controls and tests**: prove no public or internal replay interface accepts a filesystem path; fuzz any internal path construction with traversal sequences, absolute paths, URL-encoded variants and symlinks pointing outside the archive root; assert containment.
- **SAST/Semgrep rules** specific to this epic: flag any new code path that constructs a filesystem path from request-derived data, and any code that clears or overwrites the `source` marker on an event.
- **DAST/ZAP profile additions** for the replay REST surface, including authorisation-matrix probing across roles Owner / Manager / Viewer for `replay:read` and `replay:write`.
- Wire all of the above into CI as gating checks.

## Out of scope
- The threat model itself (E26-X01) and the final security review (E26-X03).
- Programme-level pen-testing.
- Fixing defects found — filed to the owning tickets with severity, and P0/P1 block E26-X03.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No path can be supplied, and none can escape
  Given every replay interface
  When traversal sequences, absolute paths, encoded variants and symlinks are attempted
  Then no interface accepts a path parameter
  And every internally constructed path is proven contained within the archive root

Scenario: Replay can never place a real order
  Given an order placed during a replay session
  When re-tagging is attempted at the API, service and OMS layers
  Then every attempt is refused on the source="replay" marker
  And method-level spies confirm zero exchange-adapter calls

Scenario: Cross-user access reveals nothing
  Given a session owned by another user
  When it is referenced over REST or WS
  Then the response is not-found or replay_session_not_found
  And the response does not distinguish a non-existent session from an unauthorised one

Scenario: Resource limits hold under abuse
  Given a quota-exceeding session burst, an oversized window and a seek storm
  Then each is rejected or coalesced before resources are committed
  And memory and task counts remain bounded throughout

Scenario: The rules prevent regression, not just today's code
  Given a new commit that builds a filesystem path from request data or clears a source marker
  Then the SAST rule fails the build
```

## Technical notes / design
The isolation test must spy at the adapter method level rather than at the network level: a network-level assertion passes trivially if the adapter is mocked in the test environment, which would make the most important test in the epic vacuous.

The cross-user tests must assert response *equivalence* between "does not exist" and "not yours", since a timing or wording difference is itself the disclosure.

## Test plan
Security tests run in the standard CI security job; the fuzzing component runs with a fixed corpus on PRs and an extended corpus nightly. Every test states the control it protects, so a failure names the invariant rather than a line number.

## Security notes
This is the epic's control-verification deliverable, mapping to SR-097, the RBAC matrix (`replay:read`/`replay:write`, scope self, per `04-security-program.md` §RBAC row and the "Use replay on recorded data" permission row), and the resource-governance limits from E26-T01.

## Accessibility notes
Includes a check that assistive-technology output and error messages do not disclose session ids, account identifiers or internal paths.

## Performance notes
The resource-limit tests reuse the E26-Q03 harness so the limits are validated at realistic load rather than against a toy workload.

## Observability
Assert the security signals defined in E26-X01 actually fire: blocked live-routing attempts, cross-user rejections, quota rejections and path-validation failures, each with an alert rule for the ones that should never occur.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every E26-X01 abuse case implemented and green.
- [ ] Path-traversal and symlink-escape tests mandatory and passing (SR-097).
- [ ] Adapter-level zero-call assertion for replay orders in place.
- [ ] Semgrep rules and the ZAP profile committed and gating in CI.
- [ ] Findings filed with severity; no P0/P1 left open into E26-X03.

## Dependencies
`E26-X01` supplies the abuse cases; `E26-T05` supplies the REST and WS surface under test.

`test/e26-replay-security`.

title: Security review and sign-off of replay and simulated-trading isolation
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires, for any epic labelled `security`, a finalised STRIDE model with findings triaged and a sign-off comment from the Security engineer; §8 makes the label mandatory regardless of whether it was applied at creation for anything touching order-placement paths — which E26-S07 does, by putting an order ticket in front of replayed market data.

This review is the last gate before E26-Q06 can record the epic QA sign-off.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Review the **shipped** implementation against the E26-X01 model: confirm every control exists where the model says it does, and that none was refactored away during implementation.
- Focused review of the **simulated-trading isolation** (E26-S07), the epic's highest-severity control:
  - `source="replay"` set at injection and non-removable downstream.
  - The OMS refusal is structural, not a UI check.
  - Replay fills persist with `is_paper=true` and `origin='replay_sim'`, in a separate replay journal, excluded from live and paper analytics by default.
  - Exports and journal promotion always carry the simulated flag; `journal.simulated_import` is audited.
  - Replay paper fills never enter the trading audit stream.
- Confirm **RBAC** enforcement: `replay:read` / `replay:write` with scope self on every operation, including the WS subscribe path, verified against the role matrix for Owner, Manager and Viewer.
- Confirm **path safety** (SR-097) in the shipped readers and that the E26-X02 tests genuinely exercise the production code path rather than a test double.
- Confirm the **resource-governance limits** are enabled by default in the shipped configuration, with their values recorded, and that disabling them requires a deliberate configuration change.
- Review SAST/SCA/secrets-scan results for the epic's code; triage each finding as fixed or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off.
- Review the security-relevant sections of ADR-0018 so the decisions are recorded where a future maintainer will look.
- Post the **sign-off comment** with residual risks, accepted risks and any follow-ups for the pre-Live pen-test scope.

## Out of scope
- Implementing fixes (filed to owning tickets; P0/P1 findings block this sign-off).
- The programme pen-test (before Live enablement, R4) — this review contributes scope to it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Controls exist where the model says they do
  Given the E26-X01 model and the shipped code
  When each control is located in the implementation
  Then every control is present at the stated layer
  And any relocated or missing control is filed as a finding

Scenario: Isolation is structural and proven
  Given the simulated-trading path
  When the reviewer traces an order from ticket to matcher
  Then the refusal to route to an exchange depends on the source marker rather than on UI state
  And the adapter-level zero-call test is confirmed to exercise production code

Scenario: Limits ship enabled
  Given the deployed default configuration
  Then session quota, window cap, memory ceiling, idle reclaim and control-call rate limits are all enabled with recorded values

Scenario: Sign-off is conditional on a clean board
  When sign-off is attempted with an open P0 or P1 security finding
  Then it is refused until the finding is fixed or accepted by the Owner with a recorded rationale
```

## Technical notes / design
Pay particular attention to the seam between E26 and E38: the paper matcher is another epic's code, and isolation depends on both sides holding their end. The review must trace the full path rather than stopping at the E26 boundary.

## Test plan
Manual review plus confirmation that the E26-X02 suite is green against production code paths; a spot re-run of the highest-severity abuse cases in the reviewer's own environment.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security sign-off for the epic and is cited in the epic DoD and in the R2 PRR.

## Accessibility notes
Confirms the disclosure-channel check from E26-X02 was executed.

## Performance notes
Confirms the resource limits validated in E26-Q03 are the ones actually shipped.

## Observability
Confirms the security signals and their alert rules are deployed and firing correctly, especially the blocked-live-routing counter, which should be permanently zero and alarmed if it is not.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Review completed against the shipped implementation; every control located or filed as a finding.
- [ ] Isolation path traced end to end across the E26/E38 seam.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets findings triaged; no P0/P1 open.
- [ ] Shipped default limits recorded on the ticket.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment posted with residual and accepted risks and pen-test follow-ups.

## Dependencies
`E26-X02` must be green; `E26-S07` is the primary subject; `E26-T07` supplies ADR-0018 and the observability the review confirms.

`chore/e26-security-review`.

- Isolation path traced end to end across the E26/E38 seam.
- SAST/SCA/secrets findings triaged; no P0/P1 open.
- Shipped default limits recorded on the ticket.
- Security engineer sign-off comment posted with residual and accepted risks and pen-test follow-ups.

**Do NOT**
- Implementing fixes (filed to owning tickets; P0/P1 findings block this sign-off).
- The programme pen-test (before Live enablement, R4) — this review contributes scope to it.
- No per-tick/hot-path logic moved into a statechart action or service (docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md §1.2).

**If blocked**
- Comment on this ticket's GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (missing contract, failing upstream gate, ambiguous acceptance criterion) and the ticket key it depends on. Move the issue's Status to **Blocked**. Do not silently work around a failing gate, widen scope, or guess at an undocumented contract — stop and wait for the blocker to clear.
